Weight-path tracking verifies regime changes (early- vs late-season); weights collapsing to near-constant is a recorded negative-result fallback to static combination.

Selective prediction with deferral-budget thresholding and messaging experiment. Bondi et al. (2022), AAAI, arXiv:2112.06751v2 (DeepMind): human-subject experiment on how communicating the deferral decision and/or the AI's uncertain prediction affects human accuracy in selective-prediction systems. Selective prediction sp(x; theta) = h(x) if defer(x; theta) else m_hat(x); deferral rule defer(x; theta) = 1[m(x) in [theta1, theta2]]. Objective: max_theta Accuracy(D; theta) subject to DeferralRate(D; theta) <= r (r = human-effort budget); thresholds chosen by brute-force grid over [0,1]^2; deferral objective weighted 0.5*sensitivity + 0.5*specificity. 2x2x2 within-subject design (198 Prolific participants, 80 deferred images each): messaging conditions NM (neither), DO (deferral-status only), PO (prediction only), BM (both); repeated-measures ANOVA. 'Conformity' metric: per-image increase in rater-model agreement from NM to PO. Data: Snapshot Serengeti camera-trap images (binary animal present/absent; ground truth from multi-rater consensus, mean Cohen's kappa 0.886; individual-vs-consensus accuracy 0.961/0.973). AI: ensemble model filtering blank images (AI-only accuracy 0.972). Experiment data: github.com/deepmind/HAI (selective prediction path). GSE ADAPT: implement deferral-budget thresholding (grid-search theta on backtested scores to trace the accuracy-deferral curve; verify deferred-region accuracy < non-deferred) and surface abstained games in the review interface as 'ENGINE ABSTAINS - low confidence' WITHOUT showing the engine's lean.

claim: Showing the AI's uncertain prediction HURTS human accuracy; deferral status alone helps. Chosen deferral model: r=1% deferral rate (1,297 of ~150k images deferred; model accuracy 0.978 on non-deferred, 0.577 on deferred - genuine complementarity). DO 61.9% vs NM 58.4% (p<0.001); deferral-status shown (DO+BM) 60.4% vs not shown (PO+NM) 57.4% (p<0.001); prediction shown 57.8% vs not shown 60.2% (p=0.003) - SHOWING THE UNCERTAIN PREDICTION HURTS. Conformity: +0.08 overall (p<0.0001); 0.116 low-confidence vs 0.045 high-confidence (p=0.014). On model-wrong images: PO human accuracy 41.9% (below chance) vs 50.6% in other conditions (p<0.001) - showing wrong predictions makes humans 8.7% worse than no message; on model-correct images showing predictions gains only 5.1%. Human-model errors correlated: agreement 69.6% where model correct vs 44.9% where model incorrect (p=0.007); human Likert scores correlate with model scores r=0.27 (p=0.021). Authors' caveat: results 'not likely to be robust across datasets, human-AI scenarios, or expertise levels'; domain-expert check showed deferral-status help replicated but interactions differed. TRUST-SIGNAL: correlated-errors guardrail - require written justification for analyst overrides on abstained picks, since reviewer and engine are weakest in exactly the same cases (agreement 44.9% where model is wrong).

Prediction-market market-making: logit price diffusion, volatility spec, and optimal quotes. Feil & Nendel (2026), arXiv:2607.17991: first stochastic-control treatment of quoting in binary prediction markets. Price = conditional probability p_t = f(L_t), logistic f; latent belief dL_t = mu dt + sigma dW_t with mu = -a*g, a = sigma^2/2 (martingale cancellation). Price SDE: dp_t = p_t(1-p_t)*sigma_tilde(t,p_t) dW_t, sigma_tilde(t,p) = sigma(t, ln(p/(1-p))). Volatility spec: sigma(t,x) = sigma_0 + sigma_1 (t/T)^eta + sigma_2/(1+x^2) - baseline + time-acceleration near settlement + uncertainty peak at p=1/2. Objective: E[X_T + q_T*Y + Phi(p_T,q_T) - gamma integral q_s^2 varsigma(s,p_s)^2 ds]; terminal penalty Phi(p,q) = -gamma_T q^2 p(1-p). Optimal quotes: pi^{b,*}(z) = (u^b)^{-1}(z), u^b(pi) = G^b(p,pi) - Lambda^b / d_pi Lambda^b; pi^{a,*} analog with +; Skew = (pi^a + pi^b)/2 - p. Solver: implicit-Euler finite-difference backward HJB on (t,p,q) grid + fixed-point contraction kappa = 4 Lambda_bar / beta. Parameters used: sigma_0=0.6, sigma_1=0.3, sigma_2=0.1, eta=3; gamma=4e-3, gamma_T=1e-3; Q=100, Delta=10. GSE port: (1) sigma(t,x) spec for in-game win-probability diffusion (fit sigma_0, sigma_1, sigma_2 per sport on play-by-play paths); (2) exposure skew rule shifting published confidence against exposure side proportional to q*p(1-p); (3) settlement penalty -gamma_T q^2 p(1-p) in pick-optimizer to penalize correlated near-50/50 legs.
equation: dp_t = p_t(1-p_t) * sigma_tilde(t,p_t) dW_t, sigma_tilde(t,p) = sigma(t, ln(p/(1-p))) | sigma(t,x) = sigma_0 + sigma_1 (t/T)^eta + sigma_2/(1+x^2) | Phi(p,q) = -gamma_T q^2 p(1-p)

claim: Optimal quotes keep ~99.4% of profit while cutting tail risk 63-87% (prediction-market MM). Monte Carlo (10,000 paths, p_0=1/2): Optimal vs myopic baseline - mean PnL 12.39 vs 12.47 (~99.4% of profit kept); std(PnL) 10.34 vs 28.11 (-63%); mean |q_T| 15.23 vs 49.37 (-69%); VaR_5% 4.20 vs 32.41 (-87%); ES_5% 9.68 vs 40.50. Spread decreases over time as k(t) rises but widens near settlement for p approx 1/2 where settlement risk peaks; spreads larger near p=1/2 at any fixed t. Skew at zero inventory: positive for p<1/2, negative for p>1/2 (asymmetric intensities); inventory shifts skew expectedly (long -> negative, short -> positive); curves converge near p->0/1 since p(1-p)->0. gamma (running) matters most early; gamma_T (terminal) most near settlement. Paper's own biggest gap: no adverse selection modeled (takers are Poisson noise); in-model evaluation only. TRUST-SIGNAL: risk reduction quantified in-model, flagged as an upper bound on real data.

Drawdown worry thresholds: duration 2.14 x SR^-2, depth 1.50 x SR^-1 (5% tail). 'You Are in a Drawdown. When Should You Start Worrying?' (arXiv:1707.01457, 2017): exact Brownian-with-drift formulas for drawdown depth and duration, reduced to simple scaling rules for a live keep/slow/stop bankroll monitor. For Brownian motion with Sharpe ratio SR, 5%-tail fits: Duration approx 2.14 x SR^-2 (years, ten-year benchmark at 257 trading days/year). Normalized depth approx 1.50 x SR^-1. Method is a monitoring statistic (worry/no-worry classification), not a predictor. Assumptions: Brownian with constant drift/vol, Gaussian i.i.d. increments, SR known. Gaussian tails understate real drawdowns by ~33% at the 90th percentile (citing 1627) - an inflation factor is needed for betting returns (discrete, heteroskedastic, regime-shifting). GSE spec: track drawdown depth/duration continuously -> trailing realized Sharpe -> 5% worry thresholds from the two fits -> dashboard GREEN / YELLOW (halve stakes) / RED (stop, run miscalibration check); ~2 days effort.
equation: Duration(5% tail) ~= 2.14 x SR^-2 (years) | Normalized depth(5% tail) ~= 1.50 x SR^-1

claim: Conformalized quantile regression (split-CQR): exact 3-step recipe and coverage theorem. Romano, Patterson & Candès (2019), NeurIPS: split-CQR fuses quantile regression's heteroskedastic adaptivity with conformal finite-sample coverage. Three steps: (1) fit q_hat_{alpha/2}, q_hat_{1-alpha/2} on proper-train; (2) calibration scores E_i = max{q_hat_lo(X_i) - Y_i, Y_i - q_hat_hi(X_i)}; (3) C_hat(x) = [q_hat_lo(x) - Q_{1-alpha}(E; I_2), q_hat_hi(x) + Q_{1-alpha}(E; I_2)], where Q is the (1-alpha)(1+1/|I_2|)-th empirical quantile. Theorem 1: P{Y_{n+1} in C_hat(X_{n+1})} >= 1-alpha under exchangeability; <= 1-alpha+1/(|I_2|+1) if scores distinct. Quantile estimators need no consistency for validity - only width/efficiency. 2,200 experiments: 11 datasets x 20 splits (80/20, equal train/calibration) x 10 methods; alpha=0.1. Table 1 (mean length/coverage): CQR-RF 1.41/90.33, CQR-NN 1.40/90.05 vs Ridge 3.06/90.03, RF 2.24/89.99, NN 2.16/89.92, unconformalized QRF 2.23/92.62, QNN 1.49/88.51 (undercovers). CQR ~30-40% shorter than absolute-residual split conformal at equal coverage. Simulated heteroskedastic: split 2.91/91.4%, CQR 1.99/91.06%. Code: github.com/yromano/cqr.
equation: E_i = max{q_hat_lo(X_i) - Y_i, Y_i - q_hat_hi(X_i)} | C_hat(x) = [q_hat_lo(x) - Q_{1-alpha}(E;I_2), q_hat_hi(x) + Q_{1-alpha}(E;I_2)] | P{Y_{n+1} in C_hat(X_{n+1})} >= 1-alpha (exchangeable); <= 1-alpha+1/(|I_2|+1) (distinct scores)

claim: GSE cqr.ts rank-clamp bug falsely certifies 90% coverage at 83.33%; exact repair recipe. The flagged bug: GSE's apps/web/lib/calibration/cqr.ts clamps rank to n-1 (rank = Math.min(Math.max(rank, 0), n-1)), falsely certifying 90% coverage at 83.33% - published intervals are 6.67pp tighter than claimed. True recipe: unclamped (1-alpha)(n+1) rank, E_i = max{q_hat_lo(X_i) - Y_i, Y_i - q_hat_hi(X_i)}. Spec: (1) repair cqr.ts to exact recipe; (2) weekly rolling calibration on engine predicted margin/total; (3) report length + coverage by favorite/dog and total buckets. Acceptance: coverage within +-1.5pp of nominal AND length <=90% of absolute-residual baseline. Caveats: guarantee is marginal (subgroups like primetime dogs can undercover at 90% headline); exchangeability breaks under regime shifts; split conformal halves effective training data; quantile crossing needs ad-hoc fix.

Proper scoring rules: Brier, log, CRPS, kernel scores; GSE evaluation doctrine. Waghmare & Ziegel (2025), ETH Zurich: foundational survey on proper scoring rules - characterization, families, and choice. Propriety: S(Q,Q) <= S(P,Q) for all P,Q (strict iff equality iff P=Q); Savage representation: every regular proper score = Bregman divergence of its entropy function. Brier: S_Brier(P,y) = (p-y)^2. Log: S_log(P,y) = -log p(y). CRPS: CRPS(P,y) = integral (F_P(x) - 1{y<=x})^2 dx. Kernel scores: S(P,y) = E_P[k(X,X')] - 2 E_P[k(X,y)] (+const) - CRPS as special case; squared MMD distances (Steinwart & Ziegel 2021; Gretton et al. 2006); energy statistics (Szekely & Rizzo 2013). Weighted/threshold-weighted scores to emphasize regions (e.g., blowout tails); minimum-score estimation (min-CRPS as robust MLE alternative). Comparative claims: log score sensitive to tail misspecification (one bad density evaluation dominates); CRPS more robust, rewards whole distribution; kernel scores choose penalized geometry; minimum-score estimators can beat MLE under misspecification. ADOPT verdict: CRPS as primary objective for margin/total distributions, Brier/log for cover probabilities. GSE state: brier.ts, brier-ece.test.ts, scoring-reliability.ts, skill-metrics.ts - Brier-centric, no CRPS, no log-score doctrine. Spec: (1) doctrine - Brier for cover probs, log score as tail diagnostic, CRPS PRIMARY for margin/total distributions; (2) implement crps.ts in apps/web/lib/calibration/ (empirical-CDF for ensembles, closed form for Gaussian); (3) minimum-CRPS training of distributional heads; (4) threshold-weighted CRPS emphasizing |margin|>14. Rejection gate: reject min-CRPS training if it degrades log-score tail diagnostics by >10%. Improvement experiment: proper-score 'skill gap' - CRPS/Brier of market-implied distributions (spreads/totals/moneylines) vs GSE's, weekly.
equation: S_Brier(P,y) = (p - y)^2 | S_log(P,y) = -log p(y) | CRPS(P,y) = integral (F_P(x) - 1{y <= x})^2 dx

claim: Paired-comparison models: Thurstone, Bradley-Terry, ordinal extensions, dependent pairwise likelihood. Varin, Cattelan & Firth (arXiv:1210.1016, 2012): review of paired-comparison models with a novel pairwise (composite) likelihood estimator for dependent comparisons - repeated judgments by the same subject inducing correlation. Thurstone: P(i beats j) = Phi(mu_i - mu_j); Bradley-Terry: P(i beats j) = exp(lambda_i)/(exp(lambda_i)+exp(lambda_j)); identification mu_4 = 0. Ordinal: cumulative link with ordered thresholds for {prefer i, no preference, prefer j}. Dependent model: Z_s = A T + e_s; T ~ N(mu, Sigma_T) (latent traits correlated), e_s ~ N(0, omega^2 I_6); diag(Sigma_T)=1, mu_4=0, omega^2=1. Pairwise log-likelihood: sum_s sum_pairs log f_2(z_{s,pair}; theta) with Godambe sandwich SEs; benchmarked vs full ML (Miwa-Hayter-Kuriki 6-D integration) and Maydeu-Olivares limited-information estimation. Simulation study 1: n=4 objects, mu=(0.5,0,-0.5,0), omega^2=1, correlated Sigma_T. Simulation study 2: mu_tilde=(-0.2,1,-1.5). Real illustration: students' paired comparisons of 6 European universities (e.g., London vs Paris: 186/26/91 prefer-first/no-preference/prefer-second). GSE actionable: build DependentBT (Bradley-Terry with subject-level random effects via pairwise likelihood + sandwich SEs) for aggregating correlated matchup judgments (analyst polls, power-rank ballots) with honest uncertainty, after a 32-team coverage simulation gate.
equation: P(i beats j) = Phi(mu_i - mu_j) | P(i beats j) = exp(lambda_i)/(exp(lambda_i)+exp(lambda_j)) | Z_s = A T + e_s; T ~ N(mu, Sigma_T), e_s ~ N(0, omega^2 I_6)

claim: Regime-dependent factor GLASSO (RD-FGL) for forecast combination with structural breaks. Lee & Seregina (arXiv:2209.01697): forecast combination that strips common factor errors via PCA, applies Graphical LASSO only to idiosyncratic precision, and adds regime-dependent breaks via kernel-weighted PCA + time-varying GL. Bates-Granger optimal weights: w = Theta iota_p / (iota_p' Theta iota_p), minimizing MSFE(w,Sigma) = w' Sigma w s.t. w' iota = 1. FGL: e_t = B f_t + eps_t; GL on residual precision Theta_hat_{eps,tau} = argmin tr(W_eps Theta_eps) - logdet(Theta_eps) + tau sum_{i!=j} gamma_hat_{ii} gamma_hat_{jj} |theta_{ij}|; Theta_hat = Theta_hat_eps - Theta_hat_eps B_hat [Theta_hat_f + B_hat' Theta_hat_eps B_hat]^{-1} B_hat' Theta_hat_eps (Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury). RD-FGL: discrete kernel K_{gamma t} = gamma*1[t<=T1] + 1[t>T1] (gamma by CV); time-varying GL with alpha sparsity + beta temporal-consistency penalty, solved by ADMM at O(p^3)/iter; Bai-Perron break detection. Theorem 1: ||w_hat - w||_1 = O_P(varrho_T d_T^2 s_T); |MSFE(w_hat,Sigma_hat)/MSFE(w,Sigma) - 1| = O_P(varrho_T d_T s_T). Data: Monte Carlo p=T^0.85, q=2 sqrt(log T), mid-sample break in B and Theta_eps; ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters, real GDP growth/inflation/unemployment, 1999-2023, p=45-59 forecasters, 2-quarter-ahead. GSE actionable: FGL/RD-FGL combiner on GSE's model forecast-error panel (PCA strip of common errors -> GL on residual precision -> Bates-Granger weights, with Bai-Perron break-aware regime weights around mid-season structural events), replacing 'last N weeks' heuristics with CV-chosen pre-break discounting.
equation: w = Theta iota_p / (iota_p' Theta iota_p) | e_t = B f_t + eps_t | Theta_hat = Theta_hat_eps - Theta_hat_eps B_hat [Theta_hat_f + B_hat' Theta_hat_eps B_hat]^{-1} B_hat' Theta_hat_eps

claim: RD-FGL cuts MSFE 60-70% vs equal weights on broken series; equal-weights puzzle explained. RD-FGL in 90% Model Confidence Set for GDP and inflation (both GFC/COVID-broken), MSFE ratios to equal weights as low as ~0.31-0.44 (60-70% MSFE reduction), ranked 1-3. For unemployment (no strong breaks) plain FGL beats RD-FGL; 'Not Sparse' (tau=0) variant among the worst - idiosyncratic sparsity is necessary. EW puzzle explained: equal weights emerge under one-factor/homogeneous-idiosyncratic structure, exactly when FGL adds value by detecting deviations. Limitations: Gaussian errors assumed (sports errors skewed/heavy-tailed); break detection near sample end unreliable; one NFL season approx 18 weeks x K models is noisy for factor estimation; forecaster panel assumed stable. Intelligence: break detection yields interpretable regime-shift dates in the model-error network - e.g., QB-injury-driven structural events (QB-BEHAVIOR-adjacent inference as event-marker input).

Hot-hand as causal dynamics: repetition heats, interruption cools, fatigue dampens (NBA free throws). Pudaite (arXiv:1801.07104, 2018): reframes the 'hot hand' as causal dynamics - repetition heats, interruption cools, fatigue/stress damp - estimated in the clean lab of NBA free throws with Bayesian hierarchical models. Model 1: Y_ijk ~ B(1, P_ijk); P_ijk = logistic(X_ijk); X_ij ~ N(mu_i, Sigma_i); (mu_i, Sigma_i) ~ Psi_1, EM-estimated (Simpson's-paradox control). Model 2: Z_ij = X_ij + Delta_h, Delta_h ~ N(0, Sigma_Delta); estimated Sigma_Delta = [[0.0402, 0.0080],[0.0080, 0.0346]] (SD 0.20/0.19 logit units, rho=0.21). Model 3: minute-binned Kalman-filtered Delta_h(t) with Mahalanobis trend statistics for fatigue/stress. Estimands: delta12 = Pct2-Pct1 (repetition), cross-trip drops (interruption), Delta_h(t) trajectories. Data: NBA play-by-play 2000-01 through 2013-14 (14 seasons), 1,233 players; Gilovich-Vallone-Tversky (1985) Celtics data re-analysis. Key identification move: condition on the act of shooting, not the outcome (methodological trust signal for hot-hand claims - distinguishes real heat from selection artifacts). GSE actionable: add repetition/interruption/fatigue features to NFL player-prop models (touch index within drive, plays since last touch, cumulative snaps, score leverage) via Bayesian hierarchical logistic, behind a numeric gate: player-adjusted within-drive repetition >= +2pp catch rate (|z|>3) AND between-drive interruption <= -1pp (|z|>2) on nflverse 2018-2024, else REJECT.
equation: P_ijk = logistic(X_ijk); X_ij ~ N(mu_i, Sigma_i); (mu_i, Sigma_i) ~ Psi_1 | Z_ij = X_ij + Delta_h; Delta_h ~ N(0, Sigma_Delta)

claim: Repetition heats +5.3pp; interruption cools; improvement continues to ~6th-7th trip (NBA FT). Repetition: 2nd FT +5.3pp over 1st on first trips (73.0% -> 78.3%, z=24.6, N=79,771); exactly-2 trips +4.6pp (73.2% -> 77.8%, z=46.56, N=382,031); 3+ trips: 78.1% -> 83.2% -> 85.0%; 46% more 1st than 3rd misses (1,016 vs 695). Interruption: 1st shot of 2nd trip 74.2% vs last of 1st trip 78.3% (cools), but above 1st-trip 1st shot 73.0% (+1.2pp retention, z=5.395). vs Arkes (2010) conditional +2.9pp (SE 0.8pp): author's unconditional repetition effect ~5-6pp, ~2x larger. Model 2: trip-to-trip displacement SD approx 3.5pp for a typical 75.4% shooter; improvement continues to ~6th-7th trip. Model 3 fatigue/stress: decline over game (Mahalanobis 3.5/2.9), steeper from minute 45 through OT - 'suggestive' only, confounded by substitution patterns. Limitations: within-trip independence assumption; interruption unoperationalized; Model 2 ignores inter-player Delta_h variation; free-throw-specific, field-goal transfer is extrapolation. QB-BEHAVIOR: QB after long bench stint; WR's 3rd target vs 1st target in a drive = heating; long bench stint = cooling. COACHING: workload/snap-count decisions via touches x cumulative-snaps fatigue interaction.

Pure ballpark effects via pairwise logistic model: batter/pitcher strength + park effect decomposition. Konaka (arXiv:2109.09287, 2021): estimates pure MLB ballpark effects via a pairwise logistic model decomposing each plate appearance into batter-team strength, pitcher-team strength, and park effect; shows ESPN's conventional park factor is confounded and degrades prediction for singles/walks. Conventional PF: PF_a^HR = [(HS_home+HA_home)/Games_home] / [(HS_road+HA_road)/Games_road]; 1.0 = neutral. Proposed: p_{i,j,k} = 1/(1+exp(-(b_i - d_j - r_k))); fit by steepest descent on squared error J = sum(p - x_l)^2; reported in ESPN units via PF_bar_k = sigma(E(b)-E(d)-r_k)/sigma(E(b)-E(d)-E(r)). Evaluation: log-loss (base 2): L = E(-x_l log2 p_l - (1-x_l) log2(1-p_l)), improvement vs constant-probability baseline. Data: 1,550,000 MLB plate appearances, 2010-2017, scraped from Baseball Reference; per-PA: batting team, pitching team, ballpark; binary outcomes HR/1B/2B/3B/BB. GSE actionable: build weather/stadium_factors.py - penalized-MLE pairwise logistic (offense o_i - defense d_j - stadium s_k) on nflverse drive data for TD/FG/explosive/punt events with sum-to-zero constraints, feeding s_k into the totals/spread engine; adopt if >= 0.003 log-loss beat over baselines on 2025 holdout with neutral-event factors approx 0.

Conventional park factor degrades singles/walks prediction; pairwise model beats it for HR/3B/H. 2017 HR: conventional Coors PF = 1.195 -> P(HR) = 1.195 x 0.03193 = 0.03816; proposed-conventional HR PF correlation = 0.81. Conventional PF improves log-loss for long hits (2B/3B/HR) but DEGRADES it for singles and walks - the home/road ratio is misspecified there. Proposed beats conventional for HR, 3B, H; tied on 2B; park effect on singles/walks found negligible. Context: Rockies' claim - a 400-ft sea-level HR -> 408 ft Atlanta -> 440 ft Denver (1,609 m altitude); bases/PA vs runs/game R^2 = 0.8522. Limitations: in-sample only (no held-out); steepest descent on squared error despite log-loss evaluation; static within-season team strengths; no identifiability constraints stated; baseball-specific event set. TRUST-SIGNAL: the singles/walks sanity check (neutral events should come out approx 0) is a structural-validity pattern reusable for any factor estimation. NFL port fills GSE's open 'no verified travel/altitude coefficient' gap (Denver altitude, domes, wind bowls).

OhmicFlow: Ohm's-law demand/impedance/flow decomposition with counterfactual voltmeter. Li, Liu & Zhao (arXiv:2608.28598, 2026): OhmicFlow forecasts transit passenger flow under extreme weather using an Ohm's-law-inspired demand/impedance/flow decomposition; the transferable trick is the counterfactual 'voltmeter' - re-running the model with disrupted inputs swapped for normal-weather references to infer latent demand. Ammeter: future-aware TFT-GAT spatiotemporal backbone predicting disrupted flow I_hat (quantiles 0.1/0.5/0.9). Voltmeter: weight-shared replica with disrupted travel time replaced by normal reference (10th percentile of historical same-hour travel time) -> counterfactual latent demand U_hat. PTC thermistor: impedance R_hat_{k,t} = R^b_{k,t} [1 + alpha_{i,t} (I^in_{i,t}/eta_{i,p})^2] + 1; Ohmic consistency loss I_hat approx U_hat/R_hat + KCL inflow-conservation supervision + priors (U >= I); R >= 1. Future-aware attention over Omega = T_h union T_f (no causal masking) so predictions consume anticipated warnings. Data: 10 years Shenzhen Metro data, 17 extreme weather events (typhoons, rainstorms); per-OD: historical flow, anticipated weather W_t, anticipated disrupted travel time tau, expected normal flow (same weekday/hour, most recent undisrupted week), static station/OD features; chronological splits (Events 1-5, 6-10, 11-14). GSE actionable: weather/counterfactual.py - train GSE's game model with weather features, then run each game twice (factual weather vs neutral 70F/5mph/no-precip); counterfactual output = weather-neutral team strength for ratings, difference = weather edge for line shopping; adopt if counterfactual ratings beat factual by >= 0.3 MAE points on 2024 holdout with correct sign on >= 60% of extreme-weather games.
equation: I_hat approx U_hat / R_hat; U >= I; R >= 1 | R_hat_{k,t} = R^b_{k,t} [1 + alpha_{i,t} (I^in_{i,t}/eta_{i,p})^2] + 1

claim: OhmicFlow beats 9 baselines on all settings; counterfactual weather trick ports to NFL totals. Beats all 9 baselines on all 3 settings: MAE gains 38.6%/18.0%/17.1%, RMSE 38.2%/13.1%/16.3%, sMAPE 31.8%/22.9%/19.0% over best baseline. Uncertainty: narrowest intervals (MPIW 13.40/12.12/12.82) with highest/near-highest coverage (PICP 93.6%/93.4%/94.8%). Ablation: Ohmic constraint is the main driver; gains scale with disruption severity (slopes < 1 vs vanilla). Transplanting Ohmic modules onto other backbones improves most of them. Worst forward-input perturbation degrades RMSE only 2.30% (weather timing) / 0.31% (travel time). Case studies (Typhoons Nida 2016, Saola 2023): captures anticipatory demand shifts before landfall warnings that baselines miss. Limitations: 17 events small; 'anticipated' times approximated from historical analogs; no public code; Shenzhen data proprietary; normal-flow reference leaks some post-event info. TRUST-SIGNAL: weather-edge (factual - counterfactual) as betting-signal diagnostic and weather-line shopping - decomposing prediction into stable strength vs weather edge.

FTR-18: transfer-rumour pipeline taxonomy and hedging-language lexicon. Dataset-construction paper proposing FTR-18, a multilingual (English/Spanish/Portuguese) corpus of 2018 summer-window football transfer news + Twitter reactions with veracity labels resolved via official UEFA registration. No classifier trained - the contribution is the rumour pipeline taxonomy (detection -> tracking -> stance -> veracity -> evidence retrieval) and the hedging-language lexicon used by journalists reporting unverified transfers. Veracity rule: rumour True iff the transfer to that destination is confirmed in the 2018 summer transfer window, or the player stays for 'staying' rumours. Collection protocol: manual rumour identification, daily semi-automated headline-filtered news harvesting, Twitter streaming-API crawl per rumour, post-window veracity labeling. Data: 3,045 news articles (1,517 EN, 747 ES, 781 PT) from 96 news organizations, June 24-August 31, 2018; 2,064K tweets (1,130K EN, 677K ES, 257K PT); 304 transfer moves involving 175 players; 12 monitored clubs (2017-18 UCL group stage: Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United, Tottenham, Atletico Madrid, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Sevilla, Benfica, Porto, Sporting CP); scrapers at github.com/dcaled/FTR-18. GSE actionable: build the five-stage rumor pipeline for NFL (injury/trade rumors) with a hedging index that down-weights rumor influence in downstream models, plus echo-graph source discounting; veracity-via-official-registration maps to official inactive lists and roster transactions as rumor ground truth.

FTR-18 qualitative: attribution hedging lexicon, echo effect, question headlines, conditional cascades. Zero experimental results (dataset scale only); veracity annotation was pending at publication. Qualitative observations: pervasive attribution hedging ('according to reports/sources,' 'linked to,' 'reports suggest'), echo effect of outlets re-reporting third-party rumours as news, question-headlines concentrated in Spanish media, cascading conditional-move narratives ('club will sell X to fund Y'). TRUST-SIGNAL: hedging lexicon as features for a rumor-confidence scorer (hedged phrasing -> lower extraction confidence); source-attribution graph to discount echo confirmations. OTHER: injury/trade rumor pipeline taxonomy (detection -> tracking -> stance -> veracity -> evidence retrieval) portable to NFL rumor desk; veracity-via-official-registration maps to official inactive lists and roster transactions as rumor ground truth.

Bandit market maker: worst-case-profit reward and regret bound. Della Penna & Reid (2012): models a profit-driven market maker as a bandit problem - the maker explores overround (margin) levels as bandit arms, prices within each round via overround-LMSR cost functions, rewarded by worst-case-profit improvement. Reward: r_q(C; s) = min_p V_{q+s}(C,p) - min_p V_q(C,p), V_q(C,p) = C(q) - <q,p>. Regret bound (Theorem 4.1, via continuous adaptive bandits): O(T^{(alpha+1)/(2alpha+1)} log^{alpha/(2alpha+1)} T) against adaptive adversaries. Reward axioms: R0 zero-calibrated, R1 path-independent, R2 overround-compatible. Simulation: EXP3 over overround arms 1.05-1.8, b=10 liquidity, 400 periods, IID uniform-belief traders, binary outcomes. Paper assumes myopic, non-strategic traders; no adverse selection modeled. GSE actionable: fit a bandit-style model to each book's historical overround path to predict margin widening/tightening for line-shopping timing; R0-R2 as a sanity filter for scoring GSE's own margin policies if it publishes fair odds.
equation: r_q(C; s) = min_p V_{q+s}(C,p) - min_p V_q(C,p); V_q(C,p) = C(q) - <q,p> | regret = O(T^{(alpha+1)/(2alpha+1)} log^{alpha/(2alpha+1)} T)

claim: Bandit maker captures 40% of max profit vs 66.7% for best fixed overround (exploration cost). Max achievable profit (omniscient fixed 1.5 overround, infinite liquidity): 100. Best fixed-overround maker: 2/3 of max (approx 66.7). EXP3 bandit maker: 2/5 of max (approx 40) - substantial exploration cost vs best fixed arm. Shock simulation: bandit maker adapts the overround after belief shift (qualitative). No predictive-accuracy metrics. TRUST-SIGNAL: the margin-setting model could inform when books are most likely to widen margin before high-uncertainty games, but the paper gives no empirical calibration to real book data.

Blackjack betting MDP under CRRA utility: wealth independence and linear stake distillation. Bordeu & Castro (2025): solves the blackjack betting policy as an MDP under CRRA/CARA expected utility - splits play into a DP-optimized round policy and a DP-optimized bet-fraction policy, proving the optimal stake fraction is independent of wealth and distilling policies into linear-in-true-count rules. CRRA utility: u_1(w; alpha) = w^alpha/alpha if alpha>0; ln(w) if alpha=0 (alpha=0 is log utility = Kelly). Theorem 1: optimal CRRA policy independent of wealth: pi*_{theta,u_1,H}(d,w,n) = pi*_{theta,u_1,H}(d,w',n) for all w,w'. Theorem 2: with infinite horizon (H->infinity), optimal policy independent of rounds played n. Value recursion: V*(psi_n=psi) = w^alpha/alpha * U*(psi) (alpha>0); ln(w) + U*(psi) (alpha=0), with U*(psi) = max_{b in [0,0.5]} sum_{x in R} sum_{d'} P(d_{n+1}=d', X_theta^d = x | d_n = d) * (1+b*x)^alpha * U*(psi'). Partial policy linear form: omega_tilde(c) approx m_j*c + k_j for true count c per risk level alpha_j. GSE actionable: build a 'GSE stake MDP' (state = edge estimate, bankroll, week) solved by finite-horizon DP and distilled to a linear per-pick staking rule b*(e) approx m*e + k per risk-aversion level.
equation: u_1(w; alpha) = w^alpha/alpha (alpha>0); ln(w) (alpha=0) | pi*_{theta,u_1,H}(d,w,n) = pi*_{theta,u_1,H}(d,w',n) for all w, w' | V*(psi_n=psi) = w^alpha/alpha * U*(psi) (alpha>0); ln(w) + U*(psi) (alpha=0)

claim: Optimized blackjack round policy beats basic strategy only slightly; wealth independence justifies bankroll-fraction staking. Optimized round policy beats basic strategy only slightly. Betting on exact deck composition slightly outperforms Hi-Lo true-count betting. 'Kelly' never appears by name (alpha->0 log case is Kelly, connection undiscussed). No external dataset: computed probability mass functions of per-round returns (basic strategy and semi-optimal round policy), Monte Carlo session simulations. OTHER: wealth-independent optimal stake fraction justifies bankroll-fraction staking rules; linear-in-edge distillation b*(e) approx m*e + k per alpha generalizes Kelly (f* = edge/odds) with a risk-aversion dial instead of fixed Kelly; acceptance gate requires beating half-Kelly on terminal log growth with max drawdown <= half-Kelly's.

Expected Maximum Score (EMS) for multi-entry tournament portfolios: submodular, SAA MILP, PROP+. Decary, Bergman, Cardonha, Imbrogno, Lodi (2024): optimizes multi-entry portfolios for top-heavy tournament pools. EMS: E[S(E)] = sum_omega P(omega) * max_{e in E} s(e,omega), approximated by (1/N) sum_n max_{e in E} s(e,omega_n). Submodularity: E[S(E union {e})] - E[S(E)] decreasing in E (diminishing returns to additional entries); greedy has (1-1/e) approximation in principle. SAA MILP: max (1/N) sum_n z_n s.t. z_n <= sum_e y_{e,n} * s(e,omega_n), entry-feasibility constraints. Training: March Madness tournaments 2017-2023 (excl. 2020), Kaggle structures, 538 Elo-based win-probability matrices; evaluation on 10,000 fresh simulated brackets per solution. Key theoretical findings: best individual entry need NOT belong to the optimal portfolio; optimal diversification increases as win probabilities approach 0.5. Exact DP infeasible: 2,548.42s for 2 entries on 64 teams. GSE actionable: build a greedy-SAA (G-SAA) DFS portfolio optimizer maximizing EMS over simulated slates, plus a field-aware variant targeting win probability against a synthetic sharp field.
equation: E[S(E)] = sum_omega P(omega) * max_{e in E} s(e,omega) | (1/N) sum_n z_n s.t. z_n <= sum_e y_{e,n} * s(e,omega_n)

claim: PROP+ 100-entry portfolio: 2.2% chance of $1M ($10K staked, $22K expected gross); simultaneous optimization beats sequential. Empirical EMS (out-of-sample, 192 max): 2 entries - SAA 105.7, SIP 103.1, G-SAA 104.7, PROP 100.1, PROP+ 105.9. 3 entries - SAA 111.5, SIP 107.9, G-SAA 110.7, PROP 103.5, PROP+ 111.5. 100 entries - PROP+ 138.62 (dominates; highest SD - desirable for top-heavy payouts). Simultaneous optimization (SAA, PROP+) beats myopic sequential (SIP). Real DK 2023 March Madness pool: PROP+ 100-entry portfolio -> 2.2% chance of winning $1M ($10,000 staked; 2.2% x $1M = $22,000 expected gross). Monte Carlo check: 250 scenarios gave worst-case 95% CI widths of 0.44 (2 entries) / 0.39 (100 entries) out of 192 points. Diversification dial: concentrate when confident, diversify when uncertain. Proposed field-aware EMS extension (maximize P(beating a synthetic sharp field)) converts the no-field-modeling limitation into a contrarian-leverage optimizer.

Classification with abstention under per-class error caps: rate-optimal bounds and additive vs product ambiguity. Theory+experiment paper on classification with abstention under separate per-class error constraints (R0 <= 0.05, R1 <= 0.05). Excess-risk upper bound: O(sqrt((d_H log n + log(1/delta))/n)) for hypothesis class with VC dimension d_H, sample size n, confidence 1-delta; matching minimax lower bound up to log factors. Feasibility pathology: under strict deterministic feasibility, excess ambiguity risk can be forced to 1 (abstain on everything); randomized prediction restores feasibility. Constraints: class-conditional errors R0 <= alpha0, R1 <= alpha1 (experiments use 0.05/0.05); objective: minimize product or additive ambiguity (abstention risk). GSE actionable: build per-market-type gate models (spread / total / moneyline as 'classes') with separate loss-rate caps and additive ambiguity minimization with randomized tie-breaking at the gate boundary to avoid degenerate all-abstain weeks; adaptive caps (tighten after drawdown weeks, relax above water) as an improvement experiment - a time-varying version of the paper's fixed caps.
equation: excess risk = O(sqrt((d_H log n + log(1/delta))/n)) | R0 <= alpha0, R1 <= alpha1; minimize ambiguity (product or additive)

claim: Product ambiguity abstains less but can violate caps; additive is the safer feasible choice. Ambiguity risk, product vs additive vs Lei baseline - Vertebral: 0.2591 vs 0.3086 vs 0.3505. MAGIC: product 0.4332 vs additive 0.5107 (both hold errors < 0.05). BCI: product (linear hinge) 0.0077 with errors R0 = 0.0505, R1 = 0.0450 vs Lei 0.2293 (~30x win). Phoneme: additive 0.5292 vs Lei 0.5606; product 0.4482 but violates with R0 = 0.0551 (over cap - infeasible). Sensorless: product 0.0166, additive 0.0644, Lei 0.2833. Synthetic: additive 0.5056 vs Lei 0.6038; product 0.4415 with errors 0.0512/0.0479 (slightly over cap). Pattern: product ambiguity usually abstains less but can violate the per-class cap; additive is the safer, usually-feasible choice. Binary classification only. Data: Vertebral, MAGIC (gamma telescope), BCI, Phoneme, Sensorless (sensorless drive diagnosis) real datasets, plus synthetic; compared vs a Lei (2014)-style baseline.

Skellam regression for score differentials: PMF, eLPAR positional value. Pelechrinis & Winston (2020, arXiv:1807.07536v5): a Skellam regression that models soccer's final score differential directly (sidestepping the negative -0.06 home-away goal correlation that breaks bivariate Poisson), producing calibrated win/draw/loss probabilities and an 'expected league points above replacement' (eLPAR) positional-value metric. Skellam PMF: P(z) = e^{-(lambda1+lambda2)} * (lambda1/lambda2)^{z/2} * I_z(2 sqrt(lambda1 lambda2)); model Z ~ Skellam(lambda1,lambda2), log(lambda1) = b1^T x, log(lambda2) = b2^T x, fit by MLE. Win/draw/loss from PMF summation. Brier: B_s = (1/N) sum_i sum_{j=1}^{R} (p_{ij} - o_{ij})^2. eLPAR: eLPAR_p(phi) = 3*deltaP_w + 1*deltaP_d; time-weighted eLPAR_p = (1/T) sum_phi t_phi * eLPAR_p(phi). Replacement level = mean FIFA rating of bottom salary decile (GK 68.3, defense 64.4, midfield 64.5, attack 67.5). Covariates: home-minus-away average FIFA rating of defensive line, midfield, attack, GK (x_D, x_M, x_A, x_GK). Validation: 80/20 random split, predicted-vs-actual differential distribution, out-of-sample Brier vs climatology, calibration curves in 0.1 bins. GSE actionable: adapt the Skellam-regression template to NFL final-margin distribution with unit-strength differentials as covariates, producing a closed-form spread/total probability surface complementary to the engine's Monte Carlo; acceptance gate: out-of-sample Brier < climatology by >=0.02 and P(cover) calibration slope in [0.9, 1.1].
equation: P(z) = e^{-(lambda1+lambda2)} * (lambda1/lambda2)^{z/2} * I_z(2 sqrt(lambda1 lambda2)) | log(lambda1) = b1^T x; log(lambda2) = b2^T x | eLPAR_p(phi) = 3*deltaP_w + 1*deltaP_d

claim: Skellam model: out-of-sample Brier 0.58 vs 0.65 climatology; same-rated defender adds most value. Coefficients (N=21,374): log(lambda1): x_D 0.01761***, x_M 0.02559***, x_A 0.00747***, x_GK 0.00142 (n.s.); log(lambda2): x_D -0.02607***, x_M -0.01759***, x_A -0.01095***, x_GK -0.00313**. Goal dispersion approx 1.01 home / 1.10 away (Poisson justified). Out-of-sample Brier 0.58 vs climatology baseline 0.65 (home 46% / away 29% / draw 25%). Calibration curves 'practically on top of the y=x line'; model never predicts draw prob >30%. eLPAR: same-rated defender adds most, then midfielder, then attacker, GK least; every EPL team underpays defenders; mean absolute salary-performance deviation approx 9.5%. Limitations flagged: random (not time-ordered) 80/20 split; NFL transfer needs key-number treatment (+-3, +-7 margin spikes) and draw-mass redistribution. TRUST-SIGNAL: calibration validation protocol (0.1-bin curves vs y=x, Brier vs climatology) directly reusable for engine win-prob QC. OTHER: covariance-free argument - Skellam PMF independent of bivariate correlation, relevant because NFL home/away scoring also shows weak correlation.

Stochastic differential theory of cricket: Brownian, wicket-shock, and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck in-play win probability. Santosh Kumar Radha (2019, arXiv:1908.07372v1): models cricket score progression as a stochastic differential equation (Brownian, wicket-shock-perturbed, and mean-reverting Ornstein-Uhlenbeck variants) yielding closed-form in-play win probability from ball-by-ball game state. Model 1 (Brownian): dX_t = mu dt + sigma dW_t; conditional win prob P(X(1)>0 | X(t1)=alpha) = 1/2[1 + erf((1 - mu(1-t1) - alpha)/(sigma sqrt(2(1-t1))))]. X(t) = net run rate - required run rate per ball. Model 2 (wicket shocks): mu(t) = mu - |mu_bar| f(w_bar, w_t), f = Poisson survival function 1 - sum_{i=0}^{x} e^{-lambda} lambda^i/i! perturbing drift after each wicket. Model 3 (OU): dX_t = (x0 x1 - x0 X_t)dt + sigma dW_t; E[X_t] = X_{t-1} e^{-x0 t} + x1(1 - e^{-x0 t}); Var[X_t] = sigma^2/(2 x0) * (1 - e^{-2 x0 t}); closed-form P(win) via eq 15. Long-run: E -> x1 (equilibrium edge), Var -> sigma^2/(2 x0). Possible sign error flagged in the paper's eq 4 (P1 form); the conditional eq 6 is the usable one. GSE actionable: build an NFL in-play SDE (score-differential vs required-pace process with OU parameters fit per team-pair from nflverse play-by-play 2015-2024, plus a turnover-shock perturbation layer) as a physics-based complement to GSE's ML in-play model, gated on beating a naive score-and-time baseline by >=0.005 Brier on 2023-2024 before any ship (~1 week).
equation: dX_t = mu dt + sigma dW_t; P(win | X(t1)=alpha) = 1/2[1 + erf((1 - mu(1-t1) - alpha)/(sigma sqrt(2(1-t1))))] | mu(t) = mu - |mu_bar| f(w_bar, w_t); f = 1 - sum_{i=0}^{x} e^{-lambda} lambda^i/i! | dX_t = (x0 x1 - x0 X_t)dt + sigma dW_t

claim: SDE cricket paper is formalism-only: zero out-of-sample validation; mean-reversion + shock shapes still transferable. No predictive validation anywhere: no out-of-sample Brier/log-loss, no baseline comparison (not even Stern 1994, which it cites). 2011 final demo: Model 3 shows India's true win probability near 0.5 throughout despite negative X(t) - headline illustration that naive state-reading misleads. Transferable structural ideas: OU mean-reversion primitive (teams press harder when ahead - morale/momentum effect) for NFL in-game modeling; Poisson-shock drift perturbation (wicket -> turnover analog) - the 'pick-six shock' probability-dip-and-relaxation shape for live win-prob product; per-team-pair volatility sigma as 'implied volatility of the game' usable for totals modeling (high-sigma matchups widen the total distribution). COACHING INFERENCE: possession-aware drift extension would encode coaching game-script (e.g., run-abandoning behavior) into mean-reversion targets. No code/data provided.

SinkhornDRL: distributional RL with entropically regularized Wasserstein (Sinkhorn) divergence. Sun et al. (2022, arXiv:2202.00769): SinkhornDRL, a distributional RL algorithm that minimizes the entropically regularized Wasserstein (Sinkhorn) divergence between current and Bellman-target return distributions - uniquely supporting multi-dimensional rewards - evaluated on 55 Atari games vs C51, QR-DQN, and MMD-DQN. Loss = Sinkhorn divergence S_epsilon(mu,nu): entropic-regularized optimal-transport distance interpolating Wasserstein (epsilon->0) and MMD-like behavior (epsilon->infinity), computed via Sinkhorn matrix-scaling iterations. Theorem 1: Sinkhorn distributional Bellman operator is contractive with factor Delta_bar_epsilon(gamma,alpha) > gamma^alpha - slower contraction than MMD-DQN, explaining slower early training. Propositions 1/2: sum-invariance and scale-sensitivity of the divergence in the RL setting. Hyperparameters: epsilon (regularization strength), L (Sinkhorn iterations), N (sample count); sensitivity ablations on Breakout and Seaquest. Return distribution represented by samples (no fixed quantiles/atoms -> avoids quantile crossing). GSE actionable: train a SinkhornDRL critic on GSE's offline weekly data with a 3-dim reward vector (settled profit, -intra-week drawdown, mean CLV), scalarizing at decision time with a user-set risk price, gated on Pareto-dominating the best scalar policy on >=2 of {ROI, max drawdown, CLV} on 2024 holdout (~3 weeks).
equation: loss = S_epsilon(mu, nu) | contraction factor Delta_bar_epsilon(gamma, alpha) > gamma^alpha

claim: SinkhornDRL SOTA on 55 Atari (mean/median/IQM); slower early training from weaker contraction. 55 Atari games: SinkhornDRL 'achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of mean, median, and IQM (5%) of HNS across most training phases' vs C51, QR-DQN, MMD-DQN; highest count of best and second-best per-game scores (Table 3, 3 seeds). Caveat: slower early-phase convergence on mean HNS, attributed to the weaker contraction factor (Theorem 1). Multi-dimensional rewards: 'significantly outperforms MMD-DQN by leveraging its ability to capture richer data geometry' (6 games). Compute: +20% average cost vs MMD-DQN. Limitations: extra hyperparameters; theoretical-to-practical connection 'remains elusive'; multi-dim tested on only 6 games vs one baseline; 40M-frame budget (not 200M). OTHER: only method in the lane handling vector-valued returns - GSE's staking decision is inherently multi-objective (weekly profit, max drawdown, CLV jointly determined by the stake vector); optimizing scalar profit alone can select stakes with bad drawdown tails. No repo work models joint outcome distributions.

TransDreamer: Transformer State-Space Model (TSSM) world model with myopic-posterior parallelization. Chen et al. (2022, arXiv:2202.09481, NeurIPS 2021 Deep RL Workshop): TransDreamer replaces Dreamer's RNN-based RSSM world model with a Transformer State-Space Model (TSSM) that attends directly over the full history of past latent states and actions, using a myopic-posterior trick to keep training parallelizable; tested on Hidden Order Discovery memory tasks vs Dreamer. TSSM: h_t = f_transformer(z_{1:t-1}, a_{1:t-1}) vs RSSM h_t = f_gru(h_{t-1}, z_{t-1}, a_{t-1}). Myopic representation model: q(z_t | x_t) approx q(z_t | h_t, x_t) - posterior independent per timestep so one transformer forward pass yields all h_{1:t} (breaks the feedback loop). Rest follows Dreamer: world-model learning -> actor-critic in imagination -> environment interaction; same ELBO + lambda-return objectives as ledger 1942. Training stabilizers: prioritized replay toward nonzero-reward trajectories; imagination from a subset K of start states (transformer memory cost forces fewer imagined trajectories); transformer frozen during agent training. Data: custom Hidden Order Discovery tasks (2D Minigrid 8x8, 3D Unity first-person; 4/5/6 colored balls, +3 reward per correct ball, 100-step episodes, partial observability); DMC and Atari tasks as memory-free controls; code built on the DreamerV2 codebase (public mirror github.com/weiqinchen7/transdreamer). GSE actionable: fold TSSM in as a candidate backbone in the GSE-Dream three-way comparison (RSSM-GRU vs TSSM-transformer vs IRIS token-LM, ledger 1944) on the nflverse 2015-2024 protocol, gated on >=10% better 2nd-half log-likelihood given 1st-half context while staying within 2x RSSM sampling throughput.

TransDreamer beats Dreamer on memory tasks (2D 4-ball: 23% vs 7% success); comparable on memory-free controls. 2D 4-ball: mean episode reward ~7 (TransDreamer) vs ~4 (Dreamer); success rate 23% vs 7%. Outperforms Dreamer in all configurations, 2D and 3D; comparable on memory-free DMC/Atari controls. World-model quality: lower or comparable foreground MSE; more accurate nonzero-reward prediction; longer contexts help TransDreamer more, while 'Dreamer's reward prediction does not improve much as the context increases.' Limitations: memory cost forces subset-K imagination (throughput hit); myopic posterior discards history in the encoder; gains shown only on toy memory tasks, not complex stochastic multi-agent dynamics. OTHER: long-memory simulation backbone - TSSM attends directly to early-game states ('this team abandoned the run in Q1', 'blitz package changed after halftime') at Q4 simulation time, where an RSSM compresses the first three quarters into a fixed vector. SCHEME INFERENCE: drive-level summary tokens with full attention within drives / sparse attention across drives is a natural NFL encoding of scheme evolution over a game. OTHER: myopic-posterior parallelization trick is reusable engineering for any transformer world model on NFL play sequences.

NOTEARS: continuous DAG learning via smooth acyclicity constraint tr(e^{W circ W}) - d = 0. Zheng, Aragam, Ravikumar & Xing (2018, arXiv:1803.01422): NOTEARS recasts score-based DAG structure learning - combinatorial and NP-hard - as continuous optimization over real matrices via a smooth acyclicity constraint h(W) = tr(e^{W circ W}) - d = 0, solved with augmented Lagrangian + L-BFGS/proximal quasi-Newton. Acyclicity characterization (Theorem 1): h(W) = tr(e^{W circ W}) - d = 0 iff W is a DAG; gradient nabla h(W) = (e^{W circ W})^T circ 2W. h quantifies 'DAG-ness' (cycle count/severity). Score: l(W; X) = (1/2n)||X - XW||_F^2 + lambda||W||_1; augmented Lagrangian L^rho = F + (rho/2)|h|^2 + alpha h, dual ascent alpha_{t+1} <- alpha_t + rho*h(W_{t+1}), stop when h < epsilon (e.g., 1e-8), typically < 10 outer iterations. Unconstrained subproblems: L-BFGS (lambda=0) or proximal quasi-Newton with closed-form coordinate updates via soft-thresholding S(c - b/a, lambda/a); active-set shrinking cost O(m^2|S| + m^3 + m|S|T); final hard threshold omega rounds to a strict DAG. Logistic-GLM extension for binary variables; ~50 lines of Python; code at github.com/xunzheng/notears. GSE actionable: run NOTEARS on an nflverse team-week panel (2015-2026, ~35 indicators) quarterly as an offline artifact, prune the game-outcome feature set to the Markov blanket of the spread-cover target with bootstrap stability >=0.6, gated on held-out 2024-2025 Brier within 0.002 of the full-feature baseline at <=60% feature count (~2 engineer-days).
equation: h(W) = tr(e^{W circ W}) - d = 0 iff W is a DAG | nabla h(W) = (e^{W circ W})^T circ 2W | l(W; X) = (1/2n)||X - XW||_F^2 + lambda||W||_1

claim: NOTEARS beats FGS on SHD uniformly; near-global-optimal at d=10; i.i.d. assumption is the sports gap. SHD: NOTEARS beats FGS uniformly; gap widest on denser scale-free (SF-4) graphs and larger d; l1 helps at n=20. FGS competitive at ER-2, 'rapidly deteriorates' at SF-4. Global-optimum comparison (Table 1, d=10, GOBNILP; Delta = NOTEARS - global): n=1000, lambda=0, ER2: 5.02 vs 4.97 (Delta=-0.05); n=1000 SF4: 5.05 vs 4.94 (Delta=-0.11); ||W_hat - W_G|| as small as 0.02-0.04 at n=1000. Sachs real data: FGS 17 edges SHD=22 vs NOTEARS 16 edges SHD=22 (tie on SHD, fewer edges). Limitations: linear SEM only (follow-up NOTEARS-MLP exists; 'Unsuitability of NOTEARS' critique re: varsortability); O(d^3)/iteration matrix exponential; i.i.d. assumption (autocorrelated sports data confuses lagged with contemporaneous effects); stationary points only; omega threshold chosen fixed/suboptimal per the authors. OTHER: new capability - principled causal feature selection for the prediction stack: learn a DAG over ~35 team-week indicators and restrict the game-outcome model to the Markov blanket of the spread-cover target (confounded leaves pruned). OTHER: NFL directionality sanity gate (e.g., pressure rate -> sack rate -> defensive EPA) doubles as a trust-signal on feature engineering. DYNOTEARS/NOTEARS-MLP improvement experiment targets the autocorrelation and threshold-effect gaps (e.g., pressure rate only matters above ~30%).

LLM causal discovery: pairwise O(n^2) vs BFS O(n) prompting with observational data in prompt. arXiv:2504.10936 (Fujitsu/TU Dresden, 2025): embeds k=100 sampled observational rows directly in the LLM prompt for causal discovery, testing two prompting strategies - pairwise (O(n^2)) and BFS traversal (O(n)) - against PC and GES baselines on BNLearn benchmark networks. Metrics: precision, recall, F1 (edge classification), NHD (normalized Hamming distance), Ratio. No new equations. Method: pairwise prompting (per-variable-pair causal decision, O(n^2) queries) vs BFS prompting (LLM proposes edges graph-traversal style, cycle-checked before insertion, O(n) queries); variants add observational data and/or Pearson correlations to the prompt. Setup: gpt-4-0125-preview, 4 queries per prompt at temperatures {0, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0}; LLM fixed at k=100 sampled rows vs baselines at n={100, 500, 1000}. Data: BNLearn benchmarks ASIA (8 vars, lung-disease diagnosis), CANCER, SURVEY (transport usage by social group); sampling strategies tried: random, cluster, systematic, adaptive K-means (no significant difference; random reported). GSE actionable: BFS-style prompting over ~35 GSE indicators with sampled team-season rows to propose candidate edges as priors for NOTEARS (ledger 1962) / PC/PCMCI+ (1963); kill pilot if anonymized-label LLM F1 < PC F1 or >50% of proposed edges fail statistical confirmation; effort ~2 engineer-days; cost gate <$0.50/edge.

BFS+observational-data prompting beats PC/GES by +0.29 to +0.44 F1; memorization leakage unaddressed. BFS+ObsData best overall: F1 0.77 vs PC 0.33 on one dataset (+0.44); 0.90 vs 0.50 on another (+0.40); consistent +0.29 to +0.44 F1 vs GES across datasets. Adding observational data: pairwise F1 0.47->0.58 (+0.11); BFS 0.66->0.77 (+0.11). Lowest NHD and Ratio for BFS+ObsData on all datasets. Pearson-correlation prompt variants help, but data-in-prompt wins. Leakage note (file's own): ASIA/CANCER/SURVEY are textbook networks likely in GPT-4's training data - margin may partly measure memorization; paper does not control for this. TRUST-SIGNAL: memorization-control gate - anonymized V1..V35 labels holdout run distinguishes data-driven value from name memorization; edges dropped unless statistically confirmed (probe battery). OTHER: LLM-based structure learning as an edge-proposal prior feeding statistical methods (NOTEARS/PC/PCMCI+), not as an oracle.

Model-based asynchronous HPO with joint (config x fidelity) GP and free fantasizing. arXiv:2003.10865 (Klein et al., 2020): model-based asynchronous hyperparameter + neural-architecture search combining async Hyperband scheduling (no sync-point waiting) with a joint Gaussian-process surrogate over (configuration x fidelity) and free 'fantasizing' of pending evaluations. Objective: x* in argmin f(x), observed y_i = f(x_i) + epsilon_i, epsilon_i ~ N(0, sigma^2). Bracket sampling: P(s) proportional (K+1)/(K-s+1) * eta^{K-s}, halving rate eta = 3 in experiments. Surrogate: joint GP with exponential-decay kernel across resource levels (models cross-fidelity correlation vs BOHB's independent TPE per fidelity); pending evaluations marginalized over GP posterior predictive ('fantasizing', nearly free while kernel hyperparameters fixed). Metric: immediate regret r_t = y_t - y* vs wall-clock time; mean +- SEM across runs. Benchmarks: tabular data tasks, image classification, NAS-Bench-101; comparators: random search, standard BO, ASHA, Hyperband, BOHB, async-HB variants. GSE actionable: async offseason HPO service with N workers pulling (config, fidelity) tasks, fidelity r = training seasons (2 -> 4 -> 8 -> full); adopt iff async reaches sync-BOHB final log-loss in <=60% of wall-clock time with 8 workers AND beats ledger-1988's 1-epoch baseline final log-loss by >=0.001.
equation: P(s) proportional (K+1)/(K-s+1) * eta^{K-s} | r_t = y_t - y*

claim: Async model-based HPO: strong anytime performance; ASHA slow to promote, early-fidelity rankings noisy. No exact numbers extracted (regret curves in figures): method shows strong anytime performance across tabular, image, and NAS benchmarks. ASHA 'slower at promoting any configuration to higher resources' and 'may initially promote suboptimal ones.' Ranking correlations between architectures at <100 epochs vs full 200 epochs are small (citing Dong et al.); random NAS configs are often decent - early-fidelity promotion decisions are noisy. GP surrogate scales cubically (fine at hundreds of configs; needs sparse approximations at thousands). Composes with ledger 1986 (FastBO efficient points as fidelity rungs), 1987 (CQR as GP-surrogate replacement), 1988 (1-epoch baseline it must beat).

DAVED: V-optimal experimental design for test-targeted data acquisition without labels. arXiv:2403.13893 (MIT/Berkeley/USC/MBZUAI, 2024): DAVED reframes data acquisition as V-optimal experimental design aimed at the buyer's unlabeled test queries - no validation labels needed, budget- and cost-aware, federated-friendly - and beats Data Shapley head-to-head. True objective: min_{w in {0,1}^n} (1/m) sum_i E[l(f_theta_hat(w)(x_i^test), y_i^test)] s.t. sum_j w_j c_j <= B (Eq. 1). V-optimal proxy: L_hat^ED(w) = (1/m) sum_i (x_i^test)^T I(w)^dagger (x_i^test), where I(w) = sum_j w_j x_j x_j^T is the Fisher information matrix (Eq. 4) - computable from X_train and X_test alone, no labels. Selection: Frank-Wolfe herding on convex relaxation, w_tilde_{t+1} = (1-alpha_t) w_tilde_t + alpha_t e_{j_t}, j_t = argmax_j(-grad_{w_j} L_hat / c_j) (Eq. 5-6); g_j = (1/m) sum_i ((x_i^test)^T P_t x_j^train)^2 (Eq. 7); Sherman-Morrison rank-one updates for P_t (Eq. 8); O(log t_0/t_0) approximation of NP-hard integer optimum. Single-step variant: top-k of sum_i [(x_i^test)^T P_0 x_j]^2 - fastest, still strong. Informal Theorem A.1: validation-based selection gap >= sigma^2 d / n_val worst case - as bad as training on the n_val validation points alone. Assumptions: shared conditional D_{y|x} between train/test; linear/eNTK feature approximation adequate; costs known; test covariates available. GSE actionable: run FW herding (or single-step) on model embeddings over historical games each week to select the training subset minimizing V-optimal proxy error on that week's slate (queries = this week's slate, unlabeled by definition; seller pool = historical games with charting costs; budget B = weekly compute/charting dollars); adopt iff it beats recency-window baseline by >=0.003 weekly ATS log-loss over 2024 season AND wins >=10 of 18 weeks.
equation: min_{w in {0,1}^n} (1/m) sum_i E[l(f_theta_hat(w)(x_i^test), y_i^test)] s.t. sum_j w_j c_j <= B | L_hat^ED(w) = (1/m) sum_i (x_i^test)^T I(w)^dagger (x_i^test); I(w) = sum_j w_j x_j x_j^T | j_t = argmax_j(-grad_{w_j} L_hat / c_j); w_tilde_{t+1} = (1-alpha_t) w_tilde_t + alpha_t e_{j_t}

claim: DAVED beats Data Shapley and random on all 5 datasets; validation-based selection can underperform random. DAVED (multi-step) best on every dataset: Gaussian 100K sellers 0.16 vs random 1.01 (Shapley/LOO exceeded runtime, N/A); MIMIC 0.37 vs random 1.38 vs Data Shapley 0.87; RSNA 171.4 vs random 283.7; Fitzpatrick 785.2 vs random 1309.1; DrugLib 9.2 vs random 21.4. Single-step DAVED second-best in most settings, fastest overall. Heterogeneous costs: multi-step DAVED wins under both sqrt(c) and c^2 (Gaussian: 0.04/0.2 vs random 2.26/77.7/288.3). Validation-based methods sometimes underperform random - the theorem's overfitting phenomenon; second-best overall is Data-OOB, the only other validation-free baseline. TRUST-SIGNAL: theorem-backed warning that validation-based selection can be worse than random in GSE's regime (small recent-game validation sets, high-dim features) - a principled calibration for trusting training-data choices. Direct upgrade of ledger 2005's Data Shapley for batch AL.

AutoComp: OODA multi-objective automated data compaction for log-structured tables. arXiv:2504.04186v1 (Microsoft/LinkedIn/UMD, 2025): AutoComp, an OODA-structured framework (Observe-Orient-Decide-Act) for automated data compaction of log-structured tables (Delta/Iceberg/Hudi) at LinkedIn scale, with multi-objective ranking math and production deployment numbers from 35K OpenHouse tables. File-count reduction trait: DeltaF_c = sum_i 1(FileSize_{i,c} < TargetFileSize_c), over candidate files below target size (e.g., 512 MB). Compute cost: GBHr_c = ExecutorMemoryGB x (DataSize_c / RewriteBytesPerHour). Min-max normalization: T'_i,c = (T_i,c - min(T_i)) / (max(T_i) - min(T_i)). MOOP scalarized score: S_c = w_1*T'_1,c - w_2*T'_2,c (weights sum to 1; experiments 0.7 file-count-reduction / 0.3 compute-cost). Production dynamic weight: w_1 = 0.5*(1 + UsedQuota/TotalQuota), tying compaction aggressiveness to HDFS namespace-quota pressure per tenant. Top-k selection: greedy fit of highest-scoring candidates within compute budget (production: 226 TBHr budget -> ~2,500 tables/iteration). Two triggering modes: optimize-after-write hooks (push) and periodic standalone service (pull); partition-scoped candidates reduce Iceberg conflict probability (conflicts observed even across disjoint partitions). GSE actionable: one maintenance script (optimize-after-write hook on weekly feature build + two metrics logged per week); compact iff DeltaF >= 10% or files-scanned-per-query doubled since last compaction; OPTIMIZE off-peak, never concurrent with builds; only if fragmentation actually materializes at GSE scale.
equation: DeltaF_c = sum_i 1(FileSize_{i,c} < TargetFileSize_c) | GBHr_c = ExecutorMemoryGB x (DataSize_c / RewriteBytesPerHour) | T'_i,c = (T_i,c - min(T_i)) / (max(T_i) - min(T_i))

claim: AutoComp production: 83% of files <128 MB pre-compaction; auto-tuning cut query time up to 2x; estimator errors 19-28%. Pre-compaction: 83% of files <128 MB on OpenHouse-managed Iceberg tables. TPC-DS SF=1000: 3% data maintenance degraded single-user runtime by 1.53x; compaction restored baseline. No-compaction baseline: file count grew ~2,640 files/hour; baseline incurred +25 min over the 5-hour limit; compaction eliminated it. Production: manual compaction shifted <128MB files 83%->62%, then stalled (month 2->3 distribution nearly unchanged); manual top-100 -> AutoComp top-10 reduced 6.59M->7.44M files (+12%) while compacting 10x fewer tables. 30-day scan-heavy workload (1,291 tables): file-count reductions correlated with lower files-scanned, query time, query cost; unscheduled tables showed recurring sawtooth re-fragmentation. open() calls declined sharply after month-4 manual compaction (tables averaging 42M small files at 64 MB avg) and kept declining with AutoComp from month 9+; pre-compaction symptom was read timeouts / thundering-herd retries. Auto-tuning: TPC-DS WP1 query time cut up to 2x with tuned thresholds; TPC-H: default (no compaction) won - compaction of full non-partitioned tables too costly; small-file-count vs entropy triggers performed comparably with tuned thresholds. Estimator error: compute cost underestimated 19% (108 predicted vs 129 TBHr actual); file-count reduction overestimated 28%. Cost scale: ~3K raw tables consume 150 TBHr/day avg, 600 TBHr/day peak - why blanket periodic compaction was infeasible. Monitoring early-warning: files-scanned-per-query and training-join latency as fragmentation canaries (expect sawtooth if hook misfires); adopt hook only if 8-week fragmentation degrades the training-path join >=20%.

LLM-as-judge constraint layer for symbolic regression (dimensional consistency + realism). arXiv:2509.03036 (Taskin/Xie/Lazebnik, 2026): embeds a frozen LLM (temperature 0) inside the symbolic-regression search loop as a domain-knowledge judge, scoring each candidate equation for dimensional consistency, simplicity, and physical realism - tested across 3 SR engines x 3 LLMs on physics ground truths. Composite loss: L = w1*e + w2*s + w3*c (Eq. 1), w_i in [0,1], sum w_i = 1; e = MSE, s = expression-tree node count, c = LLM plausibility score. LLM returns ONLY Python list [dim_corr, simp, sim, 'feedback']: dimensional consistency, simplicity, physical realism (0->1), 3 few-shot examples; final c := 1 - (c1+c2+c3)/3. Structural metric: expression tree score = 1 - d(e1,e2), recursive root-to-leaf distance handling commutativity. LLMs: Mistral 7B, Llama 2 7B, Falcon 7B (local, temp 0). SR engines: DEAP-GP (pop 100, 50 gens, crossover 0.6, mutation 0.05, tournament 3, max depth 8, early stop <0.1% over 3 gens), gplearn, PySR (Huber loss + complexity penalty, operators +-x/ exp log sin cos). Prompt ablations: 8 variants A (no context) ... H (kitchen sink; D/F/G/H disclose the ground-truth formula - circular, deliberate alignment-bias test). Data: in-silico physics, N=500 experiments each, 1% Gaussian noise (SNR approx 40 dB), SI units: dropping ball v = sqrt(2gh); SHM x(t) = A*cos(sqrt(k/m)*t + phi); damped EM wave E(t) = E0*e^(-alpha t/2)*cos(kx - omega t). Noise robustness: 1-5% noise x 3 placements (features/target/both). Code + data: github.com/bilgesi/SR-LLM-Integration. GSE actionable: add c_LLM term to PySR loss scoring bound-consistency (win-prob structurally capable of [0,1]), football realism (penalize absurd composites, reward known-structure terms), simplicity; small local Mistral-class 7B judge, temp 0, score cache by equation string; adopt iff >=80% domain-validity on Pareto front (vs <=50% without) AND validation Brier degrades <=5% AND per-generation overhead <2x.
equation: L = w1*e + w2*s + w3*c; w_i in [0,1], sum w_i = 1 | c := 1 - (c1+c2+c3)/3 | tree score = 1 - d(e1,e2)

claim: Mistral+PySR recovers ground-truth physics exactly (tree 1.00); prompt E with no answer leakage also recovers all. Every LLM-SR pair beat its no-LLM baseline on all three scenarios (Table 2). Best: Mistral + PySR - EM wave: MAE 0.030, MSE 0.003, R^2 0.99, tree score 1.00 vs PySR baseline MAE 0.150, R^2 0.88, tree 0.79. SHM: Mistral+PySR MAE 0.060, R^2 0.97, tree 1.00 vs baseline MAE 0.170. Prompt E (variable descriptions + experiment description, NO ground truth): tree score 1.00 across all 9 LLMxSR combos - exact ground-truth recovery without answer leakage. Richer prompts strictly better; Prompt A (no context) still beat baseline. Noise robustness: DEAP tree score 0.93->0.82 (1%->5% noise) vs baselines collapsing to 0.40-0.60 under combined noise at 5%. LLM ranking: Mistral > Llama 2 > Falcon; SR ranking: PySR > DEAP > gplearn. Limitations (file's own): LLM scores never human-expert-validated (gains could partly be a second simplicity term); w1,w2,w3 selection undocumented; occasional invalid LLM outputs inflate training time; adaptation risk - an LLM judging 'football realism' inherits stale/wrong priors, needs domain-specific few-shot anchors. TRUST-SIGNAL: LLM-judge term = semantic/domain-validity gate; two-judge adversarial scoring improvement (judge + critic, keep equations where both agree within 0.2) converts the unverified-judge weakness into a measurable confidence signal for which discovered equations GSE publishes.

PRoFILE: Granger-causal feature importance with contrastive loss estimator for distribution shift. arXiv:2009.14454v1 (Thiagarajan et al., LLNL/ASU, 2020): PRoFILE - a Granger-causal feature-importance estimator designed to stay faithful under distribution shift. Jointly trains an auxiliary loss estimator alongside the predictor. Contrastive loss: L_aux^C = sum max(0, -I(s_i,s_j)*(s_hat_i - s_hat_j) + gamma), where I(s_i,s_j) indicates ordering of true losses and s_hat are estimated losses. Dropout-calibration loss L_aux^DC (dropout-based calibration of the loss estimates). Granger-causal feature importance: Delta epsilon_{x,j} = epsilon_{x\{j\}} - epsilon_x (change in estimated error when feature j is masked). Fidelity metric: Delta log-odds after masking top-25% features. Data: MNIST -> USPS transfer (shift study); Cifar10 -> Cifar10-C (shift study); synthetic correlation/variance shifts; nflverse-adjacent GSE game data implied for the GSE spec. GSE spec in file: MLP predictor + contrastive head; per-game season importance = median Delta epsilon over games; shift alarm when trailing-4-week mean s_hat exceeds the training mean s_hat by > 2 sigma.
equation: L_aux^C = sum max(0, -I(s_i,s_j)*(s_hat_i - s_hat_j) + gamma) | Delta epsilon_{x,j} = epsilon_{x\{j\}} - epsilon_x

claim: PRoFILE beats LIME/SHAP/CXPlain on fidelity under shift; loss ordering more stable than absolute loss. PRoFILE outperforms LIME/SHAP/CXPlain on all fidelity benchmarks (figure-based in the paper; the file notes no tabulated absolute numbers). Method is model-agnostic: works on any trained predictor by learning a separate loss estimator, rather than requiring retraining or access to internals. Robustness mechanism: loss-ordering is easier to estimate and more stable under shift than absolute loss values, hence the contrastive pairwise objective. GSE verdict ADAPT: the paper's method is to be used as a shift-aware feature-importance layer for the engine, not adopted as the paper's literal architecture. Khora: population-scalable multi-agent world model with shared-state STBoard + action-conditioned evolution. arXiv:2608.08600 (Zhao et al., 2026): 'Khora' - a population-scalable multi-agent world model that generates consistent multi-view observations of many interacting agents. Architecture: shared-state STBoard + action-conditioned world evolution (kinematic proposal p_hat plus learned residual Delta) + geometry-guided view synthesis (paper equations 1-10). Compute cost: T approx N_v*C_render + N_a*N_v*C_proj (N_v views, N_a agents). Paper numbers: PSNR 26.2425 / SSIM 0.7130 / LPIPS 0.1789 / FID 7.7098 / FVD 36.5529 at 2 views (vs Solaris baseline 20.1465 / 0.5273 / 0.1835 / 4.3726 / 11.4263). User-study action consistency: 3.5700 vs 2.0750 without cross-agent state. Scaling: latency 107.16 -> 116.73 ms from 1 -> 80 agents; per-view FPS 37.33 -> 34.27; throughput 37.3 -> 2741.3 view-fps. Data: the paper's own multi-agent simulation environments (not NFL data). GSE spec in file: 'Khora-for-plays' - counterfactual NFL play simulator on NGS tracking; shared per-player kinematic state, learned interaction residual, what-if outcome queries (e.g., plus/minus-one-defender re-rolls); explicitly state-only, no neural video rendering.

Khora: cross-agent shared state is the decisive ingredient; near-linear scaling to 80 agents. Khora beats the Solaris baseline on every reported image/video metric (e.g., PSNR 26.24 vs 20.15, FVD 36.55 vs 11.43 - note from file: FVD direction ambiguous from file alone; reported as a comparison, not a win claim). Cross-agent shared state is the decisive ingredient: action-consistency user-study score 3.5700 with vs 2.0750 without. Near-linear scaling to 80 agents: latency only 107.16 -> 116.73 ms while throughput grows ~73x (37.3 -> 2741.3 view-fps) across views. Radar paper second pass: random-CV 99.28% vs LOSO 91.55% exposes within-subject leakage; REJECT stands. Second-pass reassessment (2026-09-26, triggered by Garrett's 'think outside the box') of arXiv 2609.23158 (Kotte et al., KAUST: 77 GHz FMCW radar + wavelet scattering transform for pre/post-exercise skin-state classification). Verdict stands at REJECT for the hardware system (n=15, no ground truth, no acquisition path), but the note extracts four transferable, radar-free components for engine R&D. Paper's numbers: NN accuracy 99.28 percent (random 10-run CV) down to 91.55 percent (LOSO), LOSO SD +-14.39, 14.6-point-wide 95 percent CI. Scattering-order discriminative-power decomposition: S0 67.9 percent, second-order 24.4 percent, first-order 7.6 percent. The random-CV vs LOSO gap (99.28 to 91.55 percent) quantifies within-subject leakage inflation; cited as a cautionary exhibit for group-out validation: props from the same game share the game outcome, so use leave-one-game-out or game-clustered bootstrap. The paper's interpretability finding: S0 low-pass energy carried 67.9 percent of discriminative power in that dataset - a property of that dataset (mean-amplitude shift between rested and exhausted subjects), not a verdict on WST as a method. Program-count implication: REJECT stands, so the paper does not count toward the 750-valuable target; a replacement full-paper read is owed (count was 585/750 at second pass). Watchlist only: mmWave vital sensing (respiration, heart-rate via micro-Doppler) is commoditizing; revisit annually; do not build, do not buy hardware.

Natural-cubic-spline age curves for positional EPA contributions (peak from spline-derivative zeros). Source notes on independent X analytics modeler @Matt_barlowe (~440 followers) who published natural-cubic-spline age curves for RB/WR/QB EPA contributions and derived each position's modeled peak age from the zero of the spline derivative. Sample: 2013-2025 (RB/QB) / 2016-2025 (WR) NFL play-by-play - 149,694 RB carries, 134,254 WR targets, 200,377 QB dropbacks. Method: natural cubic splines fitted to age-contribution to EPA; differentiated directly from stored spline bases; 94% pointwise intervals; linear tails beyond outer knots. Derivative = local slope of fitted EPA age contribution (EPA/dropback/year for QB; EPA/rush/year for RB; EPA/target/year for WR). X post: x.com/matt_barlowe/status/2101707476416557418 (Sep 20, 2026). Author's caveat: 'not a total EPA difference or a causal aging effect.' Engine-actionable: adopt peak ages as priors in the engine's player-aging/decline curves for projection blends.
equation: peak age = zero of d/d(age) [spline fit of age-contribution to EPA]

Calibration-leaf drift forensics: per-leaf z vs training base rate, Cochran's Q heterogeneity, Brier vs coin flip. Forensic calibration audit (flagged by Hermes as H-N6) proving that the 6.5-9.5 calibration leaf - a 65.86% training base rate - drifts to 57.12% in test and that the drift is not sampling noise. Methods: per-leaf z against training base rate with SE = sqrt(p(1-p)/n); Bonferroni across 5 leaves. Cochran's Q: H0 = all five leaves share one common drift, weights 1/var_i; Q = 19.57 on 4 df, heterogeneity p = 6.07e-04, I^2 = 79.6%. Leaf Brier vs 0.25 coin-flip line via paired per-observation difference d = (q-y)^2 - (0.5-y)^2 with 95% CIs; weighted leaf Brier = 0.2440 vs global mean 0.2478 (leaf model wins in aggregate by 0.0038). Rounding robustness sweep over q +- 0.00005, p +- 0.00005; 3-6 leaf INDETERMINATE from published output (statistic undefined 0/0 at q = 0.5 exactly). Data: docs/data/MARKET_CALIBRATION_2026-09-04-reproduction.txt lines 43-51 (variable-based calibration, train seasons <= 2015, evaluate 2016-2025); scripts/analytics/replay-calibration.ts:439 (global predictor constant = training-set mean). All z values are optimistic lower-bound approximations: training base rate treated as fixed (n_train not printed), so a proper two-proportion test cannot be run from the reproduction file.
equation: z = (p_test - p_train) / sqrt(p(1-p)/n) | Cochran's Q = sum_i w_i (d_i - d_bar)^2, w_i = 1/var_i | d = (q-y)^2 - (0.5-y)^2

claim: 6.5-9.5 calibration leaf confidently wrong: 65.86% train vs 57.12% test (z=-4.42) - collapse or fall back. 6.5-9.5 leaf: n=576, train base 65.86%, test actual 57.12%, Delta = -8.74 pp, z = -4.42, p = 9.7e-06 (Bonferroni p = 4.9e-05); leaf Brier 0.2526. Other four leaves show no collective drift (+0.59 pp, SE 1.05); contrast z = -4.17, p = 3.03e-05 - a uniform league-wide drift is rejected (leaves did not move together; ~80% of cross-leaf variation is real heterogeneity). Only the 10+ leaf is significantly better than the 0.25 coin-flip line (Brier 0.1979, mean d = -0.05216, 95% CI [-0.0751, -0.0292]); 3-6 leaf is indeterminate from published two-decimal output. Recommendation (not applied, owner-gated): do not use the 6.5-9.5 leaf as a calibration prior until the mechanism is understood - collapse into a neighbouring band or fall back to the global mean. Engine-actionable: yes - recommend applying the stated recommendation via the CALIBRATION_ADJUSTMENTS_ENABLED + model-freeze gate: collapse the 6.5-9.5 calibration leaf into a neighbouring band or the global mean, since the leaf is confidently wrong, not merely uninformative. Pole-polar construction: 8 exact point correspondences from a single detected circle for sports field registration. arXiv:2504.20052v1: a projective-geometry method that derives 8 exact point correspondences from a single detected circle (pole-polar construction) to rescue sports field registration on 'central views' (zoomed-in shots where learned keypoint detectors fail), evaluated on SoccerNet central-view images. Core equations: l_vanishing = E c (Eq. 4); Case 1: v = l_1 x l_vanishing (Eq. 5), l_2 = v x c (Eq. 6), l_3 = E v (Eq. 7); Case 2: l_1 = x x c (Eq. 8), v = E l_1 (Eq. 9), l_2 = v x c (Eq. 10); Case 3: center c is an eigenvector of E_2^{-1} E_1. Metrics: JaC_5 (Jaccard at 5 px), MRE = (1/N) sum_i ||H x_i - H_hat x_i||_2, CR (completeness rate). Synthetic protocol: 100 random cameras, Gaussian noise sigma in [0,25] px on ellipse points. Data: SoccerNet calibration subsets (8,565 central-view images); a new 300-image OOD set (empty smaller stadiums, no ground truth); synthetic 1080p projections from 100 random camera poses. Detectors front-loaded: PnLCalib, TVCalib (segmentation), Fitzgibbon ellipse fitting. OTHER: broadcast-frame-to-field registration (video lane only; no prediction signal). Engine-actionable: no for the prediction engine (consumes stats/charting, not broadcast video); bank the pole-polar correspondence trick only if a telestrated-video lane ever revives.

Per-frame GNN on tracking+event data predicting soccer counterattack success (CrystalConv). arXiv:2411.17450 (U.S. Soccer Federation): per-frame Graph Neural Networks on tracking + event data that predict whether a soccer counterattack will succeed; gender-specific models beat the pooled model, with fully open code and data. Graph per frame: nodes = players + ball; 10 node features (x,y; velocity x/y; speed; angle of motion; distance to goal; angle to goal; distance to ball; angle to ball; attacking flag); edge features (sin/cos inter-player angles, normalized distances); adjacency: teammates connected, all players connected to ball. Architecture: 3x CrystalConv layers -> Global Average Pool -> Dense+ReLU -> Dropout -> Sigmoid. No equations reproduced in the paper. Training: balanced 70% train (50/50), women 100 epochs / men & combined 200; evaluation: log-loss, ROC-AUC, ECE, permutation feature importance (15 shuffles/feature, AUC drop). Balanced label; imbalanced release: 210,000 frames, ~5% success. Data: StatsPerform on-ball event data + SkillCorner broadcast tracking (10 Hz, quality >=4/5), 632 games (MLS 2022, NWSL 2022, international women 2020-2022); 20,863 frames total (women: 3,720; men: 17,143). Engine-actionable: replicate the CrystalConv per-frame success GNN on NGS frames (unravelsports as template), with scheme-family-specific models vs pooled; gate on >=0.02 AUC over pooled and ECE <=0.10 after recalibration.

Gender-specific GNNs beat pooled model (women 0.48/0.83); defending-player features matter most; winger-rotation counterfactuals. Test log-loss / ROC-AUC: women 0.48 / 0.83; men 0.51 / 0.78; combined 0.56 / 0.76; naive 0.69 / 0.50 - gender-specific beats pooled on smaller samples. ECE: men 0.15, women 0.18 (the paper calls this 'well calibrated'; the reader notes it is mediocre). Top features: byline-to-byline speed and angle to goal (both genders); defending players' features matter more than attackers'. Counterfactual run search: rotating a winger's run 30 deg inward raised success 47.4% -> 49.2%; both wingers rotated together 47.4% -> 51.2%. Context: 7.5% of 2022 MLS shots came from counterattacks -> 9.7% of goals; NWSL 6.2% -> 9.5%. Limitations named: label is forward-looking (frame inherits sequence's eventual outcome - value model, not a forecast); no validation set; same-sequence frames may straddle train/test; success proxy is box entry, not goals.
