PageRank rankings beat win ratio only in a tiny early-season, low-randomness corner. Zhou et al. (2020, arXiv:2012.06366v1) is a negative result: PageRank-based sports rankings beat the plain win ratio only when randomness delta is small AND the fraction of the season played P is small; the delta threshold shrinks as P grows. Real data (18 leagues): BiPageRank beats WinRatio only at P ~0.1 or lower per league; averaged over all leagues the threshold is P = 0.035 (roughly NFL weeks 1-2), and WinRatio never loses by more than 0.03 in Kendall tau. BiPageRank >= PageRank in all settings. The vast majority of real datasets have delta > 0.15, where PageRank brings no improvement and is significantly worse for high-delta sports late season. Calibration: baseball most random, basketball least (CBA least random of 17 leagues); H in [0, 0.25]; CBA's H/delta is 5.4x baseball's. No fraction of removed/reversed upsets (eta) lets PageRank/BiPageRank beat WinRatio; WinRatio improves uniformly. Verdict recorded as REJECT: do not build PageRank-family team rankings; the only licensed window is the first ~3.5% of games with BiPageRank.
equation: P(i,j) = [1 + e^{-(f_i - f_j + H)/delta}]^{-1}; calibrated: P(i,j) = [1 + e^{-(Delta w_{i,j} + H)/delta}]^{-1}

claim: PageRank and bi-directional PageRank ranking formulas for sports leagues. PageRank with loser-to-winner edges and dangling-node correction: P_i = (1-alpha) * sum_j P_j * w_{ji} / s_j^{out} + alpha/N + ((1-alpha)/N) * sum_j P_j * delta(s_j^{out}), with alpha = 0.15. Bi-directional PageRank: S_i = P_i - Q_i, where Q_i is PageRank computed on reversed (winner-to-loser) edges. Metrics used for evaluation: Kendall tau, top-5 AUC, average computed rank of top-5 ground-truth teams.
equation: P_i = (1-alpha) * sum_j [P_j * w_{ji} / s_j^{out}] + alpha/N + ((1-alpha)/N) * sum_j [P_j * delta(s_j^{out})] | S_i = P_i - Q_i

claim: Upset propagation as the mechanism killing network rankings. Mechanism for the negative result: a single upset perturbs only two teams' win ratios but propagates through the whole PageRank network; with many upsets (high delta), the accumulation is detrimental. Power-law fitness shrinks the already-small PageRank advantage further. Real-data ground truth (final win-ratio ranking) structurally favors WinRatio, yet the early-season PageRank edge survives that bias. Recorded as a guardrail: no PageRank-family method in the ratings pipeline; only licensed use is BiPageRank on the first ~3.5% of games (NFL weeks 1-2), per the file's conditional acceptance gate. The (delta, H/delta) outcome model and calibration protocol are noted as adjacent to existing HFA/luck work.

Bayesian isotonic logistic regression with constrained B-splines (partial monotonicity). Montagna, Orani & Argiento (2019, arXiv:1909.03802v1): Bayesian isotonic logistic regression where the predictor curve f_i(s) is a B-spline with partial monotonicity enforced via a recursive epsilon-decrement prior on coefficients: beta_{i,m} := beta_{i,m-1} - eps_{i,m}, eps_{i,m}|r_e,s_e ~ Gamma(r_e/s_e^2, (r_e/s_e)^2), r_e,s_e ~ U(0,10). The first m_{L0}-k coefficients are free (rich-data region learns freely), constrained beyond L0=3. Proposition 1: a non-increasing restricted control polygon implies the spline is non-increasing on [L0,U] (proof in Appendix A). Application demonstrated on tennis serve-advantage decay vs rally length (x in [1,15], B-splines order k=4, M=9, knots (1,1,1,1,2,3,4,7,11,15,15,15,15)). Fit via Gibbs (rjags), 20,000 draws, 1,000 burn-in, thinning 20; model comparison via LPML/WAIC/DIC/RMSE. Data: point-by-point Grand Slam singles 2012+ scraped by Jeff Sackmann (R package `deuce`); ATP 145,510 rallies (130,577 short <=4 shots), WTA 81,880 (71,592 short); train 90 servers, test 50 (ATP)/49 (WTA) hold-out servers. Recorded verdict ADAPT: port the constrained-spline machinery as GSE's standard monotone probability-modeling tool (calibration curves, 4th-down conversion, completion probability); skip the tennis application.
equation: Y_{ij}|p_{ij}(x) ~ Bernoulli(p_{ij}(x)); logit p_{ij}(x) = f_i(x) + (alpha_i - alpha_j) | f_i(s) = sum_{m=1}^M beta_{i,m} b_m(s); beta_{i,m} := beta_{i,m-1} - eps_{i,m}, eps_{i,m}|r_e,s_e ~ Gamma(r_e/s_e^2, (r_e/s_e)^2) | alpha_i ~ N(alpha_0, sigma^2_alpha), sum alpha_i = 0

claim: Partial-monotonicity principle: learn freely where data rich, constrain where sparse. The core transferable doctrine from the paper: where data are rich, let the spline learn freely (unconstrained coefficients); where data are sparse (the tail), enforce monotonicity via the epsilon-decrement prior. This wins on all four model-comparison criteria and, more importantly, gives principled shape plus sparse-region uncertainty instead of fit leaps (unconstrained splines learn implausible increasing segments at intermediate rally lengths). Limitations noted: knot/L0 hand-tuned (sensitivity in unpublished thesis); Gibbs/rjags dated (NUTS-friendly for Stan); sum-to-zero identifiability awkward for streaming. GSE uses recorded: replace binned recalibration with a smooth isotonic B-spline calibration curve (P(actual win | model prob) non-decreasing with credible bands); 4th-down/2-pt conversion vs yards-to-go (monotone non-increasing, sparse at long distances - exactly the paper's sparse-tail problem); completion probability vs air yards/separation; scripted-play advantage decay over drive-play number 1-15.

Adaptive ranking lasso: Bradley-Terry with L1 penalty on pairwise ability differences. Masarotto & Varin (2012, Annals of Applied Statistics, arXiv:1301.2954v1): adaptive ranking lasso. BT model: pr(Y_ijr=1) = exp(tau h_ijr + mu_i - mu_j)/(1+exp(tau h_ijr + mu_i - mu_j)), home indicator h_ijr in {-1,0,1}, identifiability sum mu_i = 0. Estimator: argmin{-ell(mu,tau) + lambda * sum_{i<j} w_ij |mu_i - mu_j|} (Eq. 4), reformulated via theta_ij = mu_i - mu_j as a constrained ordinary lasso (generalized fused lasso with no natural order). Adaptive weights: w_ij = |muhat_i^{(mle)} - muhat_j^{(mle)}|^{-1} (Eq. 7), epsilon=1e-4 ridge stabilization for undefeated/winless teams; lambda via AIC/BIC; Augmented Lagrangian computation (section 3.2). Ties extension (used for hockey, irrelevant for NFL): cumulative-link BT pr(Y_ijr <= y) = exp(delta_y + h tau + mu_i - mu_j)/(1+exp(...)), delta_0 = -delta_1. Data: NFL regular season 2010-2011 (32 teams); NCAA men's hockey 2009-2010 via R package BradleyTerry2's `icehockey` data frame (58 teams, 1,083 matches, 125 ties/11.5%). Recorded verdict ADOPT: implement as ratings input with tier outputs (lambda via BIC, ~60-line cvxpy fit, weekly refit), gated on walk-forward tests (beat MLE-BT by >=0.005 log loss on 2016-2025; beat dynamic Elo by >=0.002; median <=2 tier changes/team/season).
equation: pr(Y_ijr=1) = exp(tau*h_ijr + mu_i - mu_j) / (1 + exp(tau*h_ijr + mu_i - mu_j)) | argmin_{mu,tau} { -ell(mu,tau) + lambda * sum_{i<j} w_ij |mu_i - mu_j| }, w_ij = |muhat_i^{(mle)} - muhat_j^{(mle)}|^{-1}

claim: Hybrid lasso-refit adds nothing; lasso without refitting is the whole gain. The hybrid (lasso group selection + MLE refit within groups) is only marginally better than plain MLE (Hybrid-AIC 135.20 mean NLL; Hybrid-BIC 131.60), supporting the adaptive ranking lasso WITHOUT refitting as the estimator to use. Limitations recorded: random-half CV within one season is not time-ordered (absolute NLLs optimistic; relative ranking stands); single season each; lambda by AIC/BIC not CV; no comparison vs Elo/Glicko or plain L2 ridge; n=32 is a small-sample regime where shrinkage trivially helps. GSE use recorded: fused-ability tiers as weekly content-ready team tiers for the edge sheet (within-tier games = pass, cross-tier games = edge); tier-membership changes as a 'tier movement' engine feature. Compared to hierarchical-BT shrinkage (paper 0611): the lasso fuses teams into data-determined tiers rather than shrinking all toward the league mean.

Strong Aggregating Algorithm (SAA) under Brier loss for expert-forecast combination. Vovk & Zhdanov (arXiv:0710.0485v2, ICML 2008): the Strong Aggregating Algorithm under Brier loss is a theoretically regret-bounded way to combine expert probability forecasts online, tested on soccer and tennis bookmaker odds. Method: maintain weights over experts updated multiplicatively with exp(-eta * loss); each round's aggregate is the Brier-mixable generalized prediction over weight-weighted expert predictions (paper section 3 construction). Optimal mixability learning rate for the Brier game: eta = 1. Regret guarantee: L_N <= min_k L_N^k + ln K - learner's cumulative Brier loss is at most the best expert's plus ln K. File's proposed GSE adaptation: weights w_k proportional to exp(-eta * cumulative Brier loss_k), eta = 1, updated online per slate, plus a 'market expert' (consensus odds) in the expert pool; proposed improvement experiment: discounted SAA weighting experts by exponentially decayed recent Brier loss instead of full-history cumulative loss (INFERENCE: file proposes it as experiment; known discounted variants of the ln K bound exist per file). Paper data: 6,473 soccer matches (2005/06-2007/08, 8 bookmakers as experts), 10,087 tennis matches (2004-2007, 4 bookmakers); implied probabilities from normalized inverse odds; access at http://vovk.net/ICML2008 (vintage 2008, availability not re-verified per file). Proposed GSE test data: 2023-2024 NFL seasons - per-game probability vectors from each GSE sub-expert + consensus market odds (Odds API), realized outcomes. Recorded verdict ADAPT: port as GSE's ensemble combiner.
equation: lambda(omega, gamma) = sum_o (gamma{o} - delta_omega{o})^2 | L_N <= min_k L_N^k + ln K | w_k proportional to exp(-eta * cumulative Brier loss_k), eta = 1

claim: Honest limits of the SAA certificate: correlated experts and shared miscalibration. Limitations recorded in the file: bookmakers as experts are highly correlated (they copy each other's lines), so best-expert-in-hindsight is a weak competitor; SAA inherits the shared miscalibration of all experts; Brier loss is symmetric, giving no special protection in the tails where betting edges live; the online protocol assumes immediate outcome revelation (frays for futures/correlated slates); 2005-2008 data predates modern market microstructure. Intelligence connections recorded: the bound gives a published, regret-bounded combiner for GSE's sub-experts (TRUST-SIGNAL-adjacent, certifying the aggregate vs the best sub-model in hindsight); the expert-correlation caveat is a TRUST finding calibrating what the certificate does not promise. Acceptance gate recorded: 2024 NFL chronological run satisfying the bound and beating a simple average by >=0.002 mean Brier.

Convolutional multi-head attention with roll padding for betting-exchange price-move forecasting. Goncalves et al. (arXiv:2510.16008, 2025): forecasting short-term price moves in Betfair betting-exchange markets with convolutional attention over market-depth multivariate time series, inside an end-to-end automated trading framework (JBet2). Architecture: split the MTS into per-variable series; 1D convolution per path (softmax, last layer 1 channel -> TimeSteps vector per variable); concatenate to a TimeSteps x Variables attention map; multi-channel stacked convolutions capture multi-scale local patterns. Novel 'roll padding': pad the VARIABLES dimension by copying from opposite sides (cylinder, not torus); the time dimension stays valid - preserves variable correlations without zero-padding distortion. Data engineering: 9 indicators (integral of price change runner/competitor, liquidity variation ask/bid, volume variation+direction, price variation from sequence start runner/competitor, WoM runner, WoM others); outlier truncation 10% of each histogram tail, normalized to [-1,1]; target = 5 equal-frequency classes (strong down/weak down/neutral/weak up/strong up, ~20% each). Rule-based market-regime decision tree: favorite? x runners x price x liquidity -> 54 categories; only 9 with >=1,200 examples trained from scratch. Architectures compared: LeNet-style 2D CNN, stacked bidirectional LSTMs, ConvLSTM2D, WaveNet2D, each with attention variants. Trading layer: prediction class -> mechanism (weak -> swing, strong -> trailing-stop); target = mean of max tick variation per class; stop-loss = 80% of target (swing) / 60% (trailing-stop). Example category #41: strong up -> trailing stop, target 6 ticks, stop 4 ticks. Data: Betfair UK To-Win Horse Racing, pre-live 10-minute window, 2 frames/sec, 2014-09-01 to 2016-08-29: 14,421 races (15-30 races/day, 3-25 runners/race); proprietary collection via Betfair API, not published; no public model weights; framework JBet2 at https://github.com/rjpg/JBet. Recorded verdict ADAPT: transfer the architecture to NFL pre-close line-move prediction (timing/CLV), not outcome prediction.
equation: Profit Back = Amount Back x (Price Back - 1); Liability Lay = Amount Lay x (Price Lay - 1) | WoM = Amounts Bid / (Amounts Bid - Amounts Ask) | c_i = sum_i alpha_i h_i, alpha_i = softmax(x_i^l)

claim: Timing-layer adaptation: judge line-move models on CLV, never ATS hit rate. Recorded adaptation for GSE: build the LSTM + Conv1D multi-head attention stack on NFL odds-history snapshots (Odds API odds history sampled 1-5 min in the 24-48h before NFL kickoff; per-game MTS of spread/total snapshots, cross-book dispersion, book count, minutes-to-kickoff, GSE predicted line, steam indicators) as a pre-close line-move direction forecaster driving a wait/bet-now timing rule. The file warns explicitly: judge it on CLV (acceptance gate >=+0.5 points mean CLV on 2024 holdout plus beating baselines by >=3 pp accuracy), NEVER on ATS hit rate - it is a timing layer, not outcome prediction. Calibration cautions recorded: extremes-biased recall (~45% on strong classes vs ~10% on weak classes) means GSE must re-derive thresholds rather than inherit the 5-class binning; the 100 GBP vs 3 GBP stake result (50 greens/39 reds vs positive-tick profit at 3 GBP) is a market-impact reality check for any timing/sizing strategy. Limitations: horse-racing pre-live microstructure only, not team sports; weak-class recall ~10%; profitability shown for ONE category over 30 days; simulation is not live (unknown queue position, no slippage/latency model); 9-indicator engineering is racing-specific.

Time-weighted Colley and Transfermarkt-value-weighted Massey ratings. Brown et al. (arXiv:2411.09085, 2024): predicting outcomes across four tiers of English soccer with time-weighted Colley and market-valuation-weighted Massey ratings (Transfermarkt crowd-sourced player values as a market prior). Colley: r_i = (w_i + 1)/(t_i + 2); (2 + t_i) r_i = 1 + (w_i - l_i)/2 + S (Eqs. 1-3). Massey: r_i - r_j = y_k (margin); M r = p; r_i = p_i/G_i + sum_j (g_ij r_j)/G_i - rating = avg point spread + avg opponent rating (Eqs. 4-6). Time-weighted Colley: W_k = exp((t_k - t_0)/(t_f - t_0)); weighted wins/totals w*_i, t*_i; (2 + t*_i) r*_i = 1 + (w*_i - l*_i)/2 + S* (Eqs. 11-14); draws discounted (no merit) improved predictions vs awarding half-wins. Transfermarkt-weighted Massey: WLS X^T W X r* = X^T W y (Eq. 16); home advantage as extra parameter y_k = r_i - r_j + r_h x_k (Eq. 17); final rating r = rhat + r_TM - equal-weighted sum of the WLS solution and the Box-Cox-transformed, [0,1]-standardized average Transfermarkt lineup value. Transfermarkt regression: ordered probit y*_ijg = (h_ig - h_jg) beta_h + (TM_ig - TM_jg) beta_TM + eps (Eq. 10), TM = log lineup market value. Evaluation: Kendall's tau = (n_c - n_d)/(n_c + n_d) for end-of-season ranking; Brier B = (p_w - w)^2 + (p_d - d)^2 + (p_l - l)^2 for match outcomes (Eq. 8). Data: English PL, Championship, League One, League Two 2010-2024: 204 unique teams, 47,198 games; standings (ESPN), match data (Football-Data.co.uk), lineup market valuations (Transfermarkt, scraped); extension to top 2 German + top 4 Scottish leagues (Scottish L1/L2 excluded - no valuations). Recorded verdict ADAPT: the transferable idea is a roster-value-weighted least-squares rating (salary/market prior + Massey solution); fresh-search replacement for rejected 2505.21275v1.
equation: (2 + t_i) r_i = 1 + (w_i - l_i)/2 + S; time-weighted: (2 + t*_i) r*_i = 1 + (w*_i - l*_i)/2 + S* | X^T W X r* = X^T W y; y_k = r_i - r_j + r_h x_k; r = rhat + r_TM | y*_ijg = (h_ig - h_jg) beta_h + (TM_ig - TM_jg) beta_TM + eps

claim: League predictability gap is team disparity, not forecasting skill; crowd-wisdom test fails. Two substantive findings. (1) The PL-vs-lower-league predictability gap DISAPPEARS after removing dominant teams (Big Six / Bayern / Old Firm) - the gap is team disparity, not forecasting skill. Same pattern in Germany/Scotland. GSE implication recorded: residualize team-strength disparity before comparing accuracy across divisions/conferences (disparity-vs-skill calibration rule). (2) The wisdom-of-crowd test FAILS: Transfermarkt values with no user discussion (lower leagues, moderator-set) predict just as well relative to odds as heavily-discussed ones; predictive power comes from values tracking salaries/contracts, not crowd wisdom. GSE implication: the market-prior signal measures contract economics, not sentiment. Also recorded: betting odds still best on Brier (0.1842 vs 0.1888) - honest baseline anchoring, odds remain the bar; Brier ordering weighted > unweighted and Massey > Colley is consistent across all leagues. Limitations: the equal 0.5 weighting of rhat and r_TM is arbitrary (authors flag weight optimization as future work); Transfermarkt values partly endogenous; lower-league valuations sparse; dominant-team removal is crude. File's proposed GSE adaptation: NFL salary-weighted Massey - time-weighted WLS Massey on nflverse margins (home term per Eq. 17) + market prior from active-roster cap dollars / positional salary z-scores (Box-Cox, standardized), combined as r = lambda*rhat + (1-lambda)*r_TM with lambda OPTIMIZED on walk-forward log-loss (not the paper's ad-hoc 0.5); proposed improvement experiment: per-team adaptive weight lambda_i = sigma(a + b*(games played)_i + c*(roster turnover)_i) fit on walk-forward log-loss (INFERENCE: untested proposal, not a paper result).

Three contest-success functions for points-based win probability: Tullock, difference, serial. Boudreaux et al. (arXiv:2201.01168, 2021): comparing contest-success functions (CSFs) from contest theory - restricted/optimized Tullock (classic Pythagorean), difference form, serial form - as estimators of MLB team quality via OLS with leave-one-out cross-validation. General Pythagorean (Tullock): EWP_{i,j} = rs_{i,j}^alpha / (rs_{i,j}^alpha + ra_{i,j}^alpha); James restricted alpha=2. Linearized Tullock: ln(1/EWP - 1) = alpha * ln(ra/rs). Difference form: EWP = 1/(1 + e^{alpha(ra-rs)}). Serial form: min(EWP, 1-EWP) = min(rs,ra)^alpha / (2 * max(rs,ra)^alpha), estimated alpha=1.032; recovered via anonymity property. Data: 390 MLB team-season observations (13 seasons x 30 teams, 2003-2015): season win proportion, runs scored, runs allowed, from ESPN (public). Summary: mean wins 80.98 (SD 11.15, range 43-105); mean runs scored 729.24 (SD 81.46); mean runs allowed 729.24 (SD 85.91). Recorded verdict ADAPT: test serial CSF as an alternative win-probability form in GSE ratings.
equation: EWP_{i,j} = rs_{i,j}^alpha / (rs_{i,j}^alpha + ra_{i,j}^alpha) | EWP = 1 / (1 + e^{alpha (ra - rs)}) | min(EWP, 1 - EWP) = min(rs, ra)^alpha / (2 * max(rs, ra)^alpha)

claim: Serial CSF dramatically beats optimized Pythagorean on LOOCV. OLS estimates of alpha: Tullock 1.859 (t vs H0=0: 50.07***, vs H0=2: 3.79***), R^2=0.866, RMSE 4.069/4.0722 wins; difference 0.00254 (t vs 0: 49.88***), R^2=0.865, RMSE 4.081; serial 1.032 (t vs 0: 52.56***, vs 2: 49.31***), R^2=0.877, RMSE 3.6836. LOOCV (train 389, validate 1, x390) root MSE: Tullock 4.0836, difference 4.0926, serial 3.6964; LOOCV MAE: 3.2807, 3.2932, 2.9357. Serial reduces root MSE ~0.39 wins vs optimized Tullock - 5x the root-MSE reduction achieved by moving from James' restricted alpha=2 to the OLS-optimized alpha. Authors' claim: estimates of team win proportion typically within ~.025 units of true win proportion (~4 wins/162 games). Limitations recorded: MLB only - not tested in other leagues (authors flag NFL/NBA as future work); serial CSF is anonymous/symmetric - cannot absorb sport-specific asymmetries (e.g., NFL home field, schedule strength) without modification; LOOCV within-sample in time (alpha estimated on full sample incl. future seasons); single-input (runs) model; NFL analog (points) is a coarser signal over 17 games vs 162. Proposed GSE adaptation: fit all three CSFs on NFL points-for/points-against (2015-2024, 320 team-seasons); adopt serial form if its LOOCV win-RMSE beats optimized Tullock by >=0.2 wins with p<0.05. Proposed improvement experiment: hierarchical Bayes extension with team-season random effects on alpha plus schedule-strength adjustment (INFERENCE: untested proposal, not a paper result).

Controlled-abstention neural network (CAN) for regression with PID-controlled abstention setpoint. Barnes & Barnes (2021), arXiv:2104.08236v1: a regression neural network that outputs (mu, sigma) and learns during training - via an abstention loss plus a PID controller on alpha - to abstain on predictions it is not skillful at, hitting a user-specified abstention setpoint. Abstention loss (Eq. 4): L(x_i) = -q_i log p_i - alpha log q_i, with q_i = min(1.0, (kappa/sigma_i)^2), kappa = P_90% of validation sigma after spin-up. Abstention rule: abstain iff sigma_i > tau, tau = coverage-setpoint percentile of validation sigma. Baseline NLL: L = -log N(y_i; mu_i, sigma_i); two-stage training (spin-up N epochs on NLL, then abstention loss). PID controller on alpha (velocity algorithm, 6-batch/192-sample evaluation windows) to hit abstention setpoints in {0.1,...,0.9}; constant-alpha variant also tested. Calibration check: standardized errors z_i = (y_i - mu_i)/sigma_i empirically approx N(0,1), justifying the (mu, sigma) probabilistic reading. Data: synthetic climate benchmark (Mamalakis et al. 2021, public): 900 grid-point SST anomaly maps, 8,000/5,000/5,000 splits; synthetic 1D example; ENSO forecasts-of-opportunity variant (29% true opportunity fraction); corrupt-inputs variant (30% corrupted). No real or sports data. Recorded verdict ADAPT to GSE's totals/margin regression head as a publish/don't-publish gate.
equation: L(x_i) = -q_i log p_i - alpha log q_i, q_i = min(1.0, (kappa/sigma_i)^2) | z_i = (y_i - mu_i)/sigma_i

claim: Abstention-gated regression head as an honest calibrated no-pick mechanism for totals. Intelligence connections recorded: the abstention-gated regression head for totals/margin - publish pick only when sigma <= tau - gives GSE an honest calibrated 'no-pick' mechanism for totals instead of the informal confidence filter (TRUST-SIGNAL). The baseline NLL (mu, sigma) training plus post-hoc sigma thresholding is itself strong ('a simple yet powerful method') - the cheaper fallback if CAN's PID machinery doesn't beat it. Distribution-shift caution: percentile thresholds (tau, kappa) frozen on validation sigma break under distribution shift across NFL seasons - tau must be recalibrated each season. Recorded acceptance gate: add a softplus sigma output to the totals/margin regression head, train with NLL spin-up then the abstention loss with PID-controlled alpha toward GSE's target non-publish fraction, backtest on nflverse 2010-2025 (train <=2023, validate 2024, test 2025) vs the post-hoc-sigma-threshold baseline; gate: >=0.5-point MAE gain on covered set with calibrated sigma (z-score mean +-0.2, std 0.8-1.2).

MC-Dropout variance selective-prediction layer for knowledge-tracing models. Mitton et al. (2026), arXiv:2509.21514v4: adds a no-retraining 'selective prediction layer' to deployed knowledge-tracing models using MC-Dropout variance as the abstention signal. Selective layer: M=100 stochastic forward passes with dropout active at inference; total uncertainty = entropy of aggregated predictive distribution; selective signal = std/variance of predictions across MC samples; abstain the most-uncertain fraction to hit target coverage (c=0.80). Predictive entropy: H = -sum_k pbar_k log pbar_k, pbar_k = (1/M) sum_m p_k^(m). BALD epistemic uncertainty = total entropy - mean MC-sample entropy; nested regression R^2 of epistemic uncertainty on (difficulty, +ability, +IRT ambiguity, +curriculum coverage). IRT baseline: 2PL IRT, ability theta fit per student from first 30 questions via MLE, abstention signal 1-2|p_IRT-0.5|. 95% bootstrap CIs (200 resamples) on all lift numbers. Data: Eedi mathematics learning-platform dataset (not public): 4,257 questions, 11,994 train students / 1,199,266 interactions, 1,493 validation students / 149,278 interactions, student-disjoint splits, >=100 responses/student. Recorded verdict ADAPT as a fourth GSE abstention mechanism alongside conformal/Mondrian, BALToR, and disagreement signals.
equation: H = -sum_k pbar_k log pbar_k, pbar_k = (1/M) sum_m p_k^(m) | BALD epistemic = total entropy - mean MC-sample entropy | abstention signal (IRT) = 1 - 2|p_IRT - 0.5|

claim: BALD decomposition lesson: heuristic proxies cannot recover model-native epistemic uncertainty. Via BALD decomposition, classical heuristic proxies (difficulty, ability, IRT ambiguity, curriculum coverage) explain at most ~3.8% of the MC-Dropout epistemic signal linearly (nonlinear RF bound 9.8-23.2%; 76.8-90.2% residual unexplained). Recorded lesson for GSE: heuristic proxies (matchup difficulty, consensus) cannot recover model-native epistemic uncertainty, so GSE should not trust difficulty/consensus-style heuristics as abstention signals (TRUST-SIGNAL). Recorded fairness analogue: check deferral rate across sports/leagues and spread-size quartiles so the abstainer does not just defer the hardest games. Paper flags deep ensembles and temperature-scaled softmax as stronger baselines it did NOT test - open comparison to run. Recorded acceptance: implement MC-Dropout variance (or seed-disagreement for non-dropout models) per candidate pick, defer top-uncertain fraction to c=0.80, backtest on 2024-2025 picks vs no-abstention and vs |p-0.5| heuristic; acceptance: >=1.5 pp hit-rate lift and >=1.0 pp over heuristic with deferred/kept error ratio >=1.3.

SplineCalib: non-parametric logistic regression of outcomes on natural-cubic-spline score expansions. Lucena (2018), arXiv:1809.07751: SplineCalib - non-parametric logistic regression of calibration-set outcomes on natural-cubic-spline expansions of model scores, with a compact-logit pre-transform for overconfident models, a one-vs-rest multi-class extension, and a cross-validated variant that conserves training data. Loss: J(f) = -sum_i [y_i log f(x_i) + (1-y_i) log(1-f(x_i))] + (1/2) lambda integral f''(t) dt (Eq. 1). Algorithm 1: sample 200 knots from unique score values; expand into natural cubic spline basis N_1=1, N_2=x, N_{k+2}(x)=d_k(x)-d_{K-1}(x) with d_k(x)=[(x-phi_k)_+^3-(x-phi_K)_+^3]/(phi_K-phi_k); CV-L2 logistic regression over lambda choosing lambda* by CV log-loss; f(z)=logistic(X_natural(z) . betahat). Compact logit (Algorithm 2): G_eps(x) = ((1-2eps)/(2 log((1-eps)/eps))) . log(x/(1-x)) + 1/2 for x in [eps,1-eps], x otherwise; eps = 10^(r-1), r = floor(log10(min(1-p_i))). Multi-class (Algorithm 3): fit per one-vs-rest column then renormalize f_i(x_i)/sum_j f_j(x_j). Cross-validated calibration (Algorithm 4): 5-fold models, stack out-of-fold predictions into calibration set, fit calibrator, train final model on full data. Code: `ml-insights` package (pip install ml_insights), notebooks at https://github.com/numeristical/introspective. Data: MIMIC-III ICU mortality (59,726 stays, public); UCI Adult/Census Income (32,561 train / 16,281 test, public); CIFAR-10 (50,000/10,000, public, Keras example CNN trained 800 epochs). Recorded verdict ADAPT as a direct upgrade over Platt/isotonic for GSE's probability outputs.
equation: J(f) = -sum_i [y_i log f(x_i) + (1-y_i) log(1-f(x_i))] + (1/2) lambda integral f''(t) dt | N_1=1, N_2=x, N_{k+2}(x)=d_k(x)-d_{K-1}(x), d_k(x)=[(x-phi_k)_+^3-(x-phi_K)_+^3]/(phi_K-phi_k) | G_eps(x) = ((1-2eps)/(2 log((1-eps)/eps))) . log(x/(1-x)) + 1/2 for x in [eps,1-eps], eps = 10^(r-1), r = floor(log10(min(1-p_i)))

claim: SplineCalib adoption plan with regime-dependence caution. Recorded plan: build a stateless post-hoc SplineCalib layer (200-knot natural-spline CV-logistic + compact-logit variant) on GSE win/spread/total probabilities over rolling 2-3-season time-ordered windows; acceptance: >=1% relative log-loss reduction vs current calibrator on BOTH spread and total markets with no ROI regression on posted picks. Improvement experiment recorded: fit separate spline calibrators per conditioning bin (favorite/underdog, home/away, high/low total) as a Mondrian-style combination, testing whether miscalibration is regime-dependent. Caveats recorded: paper reports no CIs on log-loss gains; CIFAR accuracy gains are small (+0.24pp, +0.18pp); no time-series validation - NFL non-stationarity requires time-ordered splits.

Train ML ensembles on almost-fair CRPS instead of MSE (AIFS-CRPS). Lang et al. (ECMWF, 2024), arXiv:2412.15832: trains a machine-learned weather ensemble directly on a proper-score loss (almost-fair CRPS, alpha=0.95) instead of MSE, preserving realistic variability and beating the 9km physics-based IFS ensemble by 5-20% on most variables. CRPS({x_j},y) = (1/M) sum_j|x_j-y| - (1/2M^2) sum_{j,k}|x_j-x_k|; fair CRPS replaces 1/2M^2 with 1/2M(M-1). afCRPS_alpha = alpha*fCRPS + (1-alpha)*CRPS = (1/M) sum_j|x_j-y| - (1-eps)/(2M(M-1)) sum_{j,k}|x_j-x_k|, eps=(1-alpha)/M, alpha=0.95. Positive-terms rearrangement (Eq. 4, fp16-stability fix): afCRPS_alpha = (1/2M(M-1)) sum_j sum_{k!=j} (|x_j-y|+|x_k-y|-(1-eps)|x_j-x_k|), non-negative per term by triangle inequality for eps>=0. Degeneracy fix rationale: pure fCRPS has a degeneracy - if M-1 members equal the observation, the remaining member is unconstrained (zero gradient); the (1-alpha) CRPS admixture removes it. Per-variable loss scaling + pressure-dependent weighting w_pl = plev/1000 (min 0.2); AIFS graph-transformer trained in 4 stages (300k/60k/~45k iterations, AdamW beta 0.9/0.95, wd 0.1). Data: ERA5 reanalysis (N320 ~31km; O96 ~1 deg); operational IFS analysis; verification ECMWF analysis + radiosonde + SYNOP, forecasts initialized 00/12 UTC 2024-02-01 to 2024-09-30. Weather domain only. Recorded verdict ADAPT: transfer the afCRPS loss (with degeneracy fix and fp16-safe formulation) to GSE's probabilistic total/margin distribution models.
equation: CRPS({x_j},y) = (1/M) sum_j|x_j-y| - (1/2M^2) sum_{j,k}|x_j-x_k|; fair CRPS: 1/2M(M-1) | afCRPS_alpha = alpha*fCRPS + (1-alpha)*CRPS = (1/M) sum_j|x_j-y| - (1-eps)/(2M(M-1)) sum_{j,k}|x_j-x_k|, eps=(1-alpha)/M, alpha=0.95 | afCRPS_alpha = (1/2M(M-1)) sum_j sum_{k!=j} (|x_j-y|+|x_k-y|-(1-eps)|x_j-x_k|)

claim: afCRPS adoption for GSE total/margin distributions with degeneracy rejection trigger. Recorded adoption: train GSE probabilistic total/margin models on afCRPS (alpha=0.95) over a small seed ensemble (M=8-16) instead of MSE - MSE training smooths away the very variability a proper forecast needs; GSE's calibration map lists CRPS as a metric but training-on-CRPS is not in the map. Acceptance: >=2% holdout CRPS improvement with equal-or-better calibration (PIT uniformity), no ensemble collapse. Rejection trigger: monitor effective ensemble variance during training - the degeneracy pathology (spread -> 0) is the rejection trigger. Improvement experiment recorded: combine afCRPS with threshold-weighted twCRPS from [0746] for tail emphasis on 90th-percentile total/margin events; neither paper tries the combination.

Correspondence-analysis mining of player strength/weakness rules from unstructured sports commentary. An arXiv 2024 (IIT Guwahati) paper applying correspondence analysis (CA) to 1,088,570 ball-by-ball cricket short-text commentaries to mine per-player strength/weakness 'rules' (e.g., 'Smith attacks leg-stump deliveries') and cluster similar players via t-SNE on rule vectors. Confrontation matrix N (batting-response x bowling-delivery co-occurrence from unigram/bigram features; 19 batting x 12 bowling features). Dependency via independence-axiom violation: P(bf intersect wf) = alpha*P(bf)*P(wf); alpha=1 independent, alpha<1 dependent. Correspondence Analysis: SVD of normalized, centered N -> principal components F (batting), G (bowling); minimizes sum of squared distances of feature points to reduced subspace. Strength rule (batsman): batting feature = attacked; bowling partner = argmax_j <F_attacked, G_j>; weakness rule mirrored (beaten). Bowler rules mirrored (strength = opponent beaten). t-SNE on 31-dim per-player rule vectors for similar-strength/similar-weakness clustering; contribution biplots for visualization. Data: 1,088,570 international cricket ball-by-ball commentaries; 264 batsmen + 264 bowlers from 12 countries; data, code, results for 500+ players stated as publicly available (links in paper). Expert ground truth: Sanjay Manjrekar ESPNCricinfo video (2017-06-01). Recorded verdict ADAPT as an NLP template: mine unstructured text (play-by-play descriptions, beat-writer reports) for per-player tendency rules instead of relying only on structured box scores.
equation: P(bf intersect wf) = alpha * P(bf) * P(wf) | strength rule: bowling partner = argmax_j <F_attacked, G_j>

claim: NFL tendency-rule miner from play descriptions with Procrustes stability gate. Recorded NFL ports: tendency-rule mining from text ports to NFL - nflverse play descriptions -> per-player strength/weakness rules, e.g. WR weakness-vs-CB strength matchups predicting target-share shortfalls (SCHEME); similar-player clustering on rule vectors -> comp-based DFS/prop projections, cheap comps with same tendency profile (OTHER); beat-writer/injury-report text -> availability signals (TRUST-SIGNAL). Recorded acceptance: build a CA-based tendency-rule miner on nflverse play-by-play descriptions (>=150 routes/season) extracting top-2 strength/weakness rules per player with Procrustes cross-season stability gate (median Delta^2 <= 0.35).

Postprocessing point forecasts into probabilistic forecasts: QRA, CP, IDR comparison with Shapley decomposition. Lipiecki, Uniejewski, Weron (Energy Economics, arXiv 2404.02270v2): comparing three postprocessing schemes - Quantile Regression Averaging (QRA), Conformal Prediction (CP), Isotonic Distributional Regression (IDR) - for converting point forecasts into probabilistic forecasts on German/Spanish day-ahead electricity prices, including a Shapley decomposition of the winning ensemble. QRA: qhat(alpha|phat) = [1, phat^ave] . beta_alpha, beta from pinball-loss minimization (most compute-intensive). CP: symmetric prediction intervals from absolute-error nonconformity scores in rolling calibration windows. IDR (Henzi et al. 2021): (Fhat_1(z),...,Fhat_m(z)) = argmin sum(eta_i - 1{p_{i,h} <= z})^2 s.t. eta_1 >= ... >= eta_m, eta_i in [0,1]; abridged pool-adjacent-violators algorithm; linear interpolation between sorted point forecasts; extrapolation clamps to endpoints. Ensemble LEAR-Ave: vertical averaging of the three predictive distributions over calibration windows m in {28, 56, 91, 182}. Evaluation: CRPS (99 percentiles), skill score SS = 1 - sum CRPS^model / sum CRPS^{LEAR-N} over rolling 182-day windows, APS_20 (extreme 20 percentiles), CPA test (Giacomini-White 2006) with Delta_d = phi' X_{d-1} + eps_d. Benchmarks: Naive-1N, Naive-N, LEAR-N (Gaussian errors), DDNN-JSU (Johnson's SU distributional neural nets). Data: ENTSO-E Transparency (day-ahead load + wind/solar forecasts), Investing.com (EUA carbon, TTF gas, Brent crude, API2 coal closes); German (BZN|DE-LU) and Spanish (BZN|ES) day-ahead prices 2015-01-01 to 2023-12-31; 4.5-year out-of-sample test 2019-06-27 to 2023-12-31 covering COVID and the Ukraine-war energy crisis. PostForecasts.jl (Julia, github.com/lipiecki/PostForecasts.jl); DDNN: github.com/gmarcjasz/distributionalnn. Recorded verdict ADAPT: the point-prediction -> calibrated-distribution recipe the GSE engine's uncertainty lane needs.
equation: qhat(alpha|phat) = [1, phat^ave] . beta_alpha | (Fhat_1(z),...,Fhat_m(z)) = argmin sum_i (eta_i - 1{p_{i,h} <= z})^2 s.t. eta_1 >= ... >= eta_m, eta_i in [0,1] | SS = 1 - sum CRPS^model / sum CRPS^{LEAR-N}

claim: Uncertainty-stack design principle: ensemble methods, volatile components as diversifiers. Recorded principles: IDR postprocessing converts GSE's point predictions into calibrated distributions using only recent (forecast, realization) pairs - no neural net, retrainable daily. The most volatile component (IDR) was the most valuable diversifier (Shapley >75%): design principle - build the uncertainty stack as an ensemble, not a single method. Tails (APS_20) are where IDR's evidence is weakest; for GSE, tail calibration (extreme spreads/totals) is the high-value case (TRUST-SIGNAL). Recorded gate: postprocess each pick probability with IDR on rolling m-day windows of (engine prob, outcome) pairs, vertically averaged with QRA + CP; gate with CPA test vs Gaussian benchmark and IDR Shapley share > 40% on GSE's 3,411 `picks` records.

Parimutuel permutation betting theory: no empirical content, rejected for GSE. Agrawal, Wang, Ye (2008): pure theory/complexity paper on parimutuel call-auction betting over permutation outcome spaces (n! outcomes): proposes 'Proportional Betting' with polynomial-time pricing via a convex program, and reconstructs a joint distribution over rankings from marginal prices via maximum entropy. Verdict recorded as REJECT - zero empirical results, no data, and GSE is a pick publisher, not an exchange operator. Complexity results recorded: CPCAM primal max pi'x - r + mu sum theta_i log s_i s.t. sum_k a_ik x_k + s_i = r, parimutuel prices = dual variables; Proportional betting compact LP: max pi'x - e'v - e'w s.t. v_i+w_j >= sum_k(x_k A_k)_{ij} (polynomial via matching-polytope integrality); max-entropy joint: min sum_sigma p_sigma log p_sigma s.t. sum_sigma p_sigma M_sigma = Q -> p_sigma = e^{Y . M_sigma - 1}, n^2-parameter exponential-family form; exact computation #P-hard (reduction from (0,1)-matrix permanent); (1-eps)-FPTAS in poly(n,1/eps,1/q_min) via Sinclair Jerrum-Vigoda permanent approximation; fixed-reward matching NP-hard (MAX-2-SAT reduction, Theorem 3.1); proportional-betting pricing polynomial with unique doubly-stochastic marginal price matrix Q (Theorem 4.4). Organizer problem polynomial (O(n^2+m) variables/constraints). No numerical results of any kind. Conditional-only use: if GSE ever runs a subscriber prediction contest with parimutuel payouts, Theorem 4.4 is the pricing design reference; the max-entropy-from-marginals trick is superseded by GSE's existing Monte Carlo simulation for joint outcomes.
equation: max pi'x - r + mu sum_i theta_i log s_i  s.t. sum_k a_ik x_k + s_i = r | p_sigma = e^{Y . M_sigma - 1}  s.t. sum_sigma p_sigma M_sigma = Q

claim: Constrained generalized multivariate Kelly for sizing correlated bets. Vukcevic, Keser (arXiv 2024): derives the constrained generalized multivariate Kelly solution for sizing a small set of simultaneous correlated bets, with long-only, leverage-cap, per-position-max, and permanent-capital-loss constraints solved exactly via Newton-Raphson over active-constraint combinations; validated on constructed scenarios only. Core first-order condition (quoted exactly): sum_i p_i k_{ij} / (1 + sum_j f_j k_{ij}) = 0, solved for fraction vector f via Newton-Raphson over discrete joint outcomes with probabilities p_i and payoff vectors k_{ij}. Constraints: long-only (f_j >= 0), leverage cap (sum f_j <= 1), max allocation per position, permanent-capital-loss constraint P(loss >= K) <= P - enforced by enumerating all 2^{N_l} active/inactive constraint combinations and keeping the feasible optimum. Log-growth objective; assumes known outcome probabilities, fully enumerated discrete joint outcome space, log utility, simultaneous resolution, no sequential rebalancing. Implemented in Rust crate `charlie` (GitLab links stated in paper). No empirical dataset - validation is constructed scenarios: five identical 50%-loss/100%-gain 50/50 candidates; a 5-asset example portfolio (A-E) with stated edge and loss parameters. Recorded verdict ADAPT: the first fully-read multivariate Kelly treatment in the repo, directly applicable to sizing a small set of correlated GSE edges.
equation: sum_i p_i k_{ij} / (1 + sum_j f_j k_{ij}) = 0 | P(loss >= K) <= P

claim: Multivariate Kelly adoption with drawdown gate and P(loss>=K) public guardrail. Recorded plan: port to Python (scipy Newton/SLSQP, N <= 10 with constraint enumeration, SLSQP on log-growth for larger N) fed by engine win probabilities and odds -> payoff multiples, with long-only / no-leverage / 25%-per-pick / P=1%-K=30% constraints; gate ADOPT on walk-forward max drawdown <= 0.25-Kelly drawdown at comparable ROI. The P(loss >= K) <= P constraint is recorded as the honest public-bankroll guardrail (max drawdown control). Replaces naive flat stakes or single-bet Kelly for a small set of correlated GSE picks.

News co-occurrence network with Louvain communities and entity-level sentiment event study. Wan et al., arXiv:2011.06430v2: builds a news co-occurrence network of 87 companies from 7 years of Reuters news, applies Louvain community detection and entity-level sentiment, and runs an event study showing sentiment shocks propagate to network neighbors and coincide with significant abnormal returns/volatility (Mann-Whitney, p<0.01). Louvain modularity (quoted): Q = (1/2m) sum_{i,j} (e_{ij} - k_i k_j / 2m) delta(C_i, C_j). Edge weight e_{ij} = cosine similarity of news-coverage row vectors (company x article counts). Volatility proxy (quoted): sigma(t) approx |log(P(t)/P(t-1))|. Event study: sentiment events -> group sentiment change and CAR vs H0=0 via Mann-Whitney U (red p<0.01, orange 0.01<=p<0.05); post-event volatility vs stationary pre-event distribution. Entity extraction via NCRF++ NER (char-CNN + word-LSTM + CRF, trained on CoNLL 2003). Data: Reuters financial news 2007-2013 (27 quarters); daily Bloomberg prices for the 87 companies; 9 Bloomberg sectors as reference; NER via NCRF++; no code or data links (Gephi for visualization). Reuters/Bloomberg proprietary - method replicable on any news+price feed. Recorded verdict ADAPT: the network-diffusion framing ports to NFL news (a QB injury story moving teammates' and opponents' betting markets).
equation: Q = (1/2m) sum_{i,j} (e_{ij} - k_i k_j / 2m) delta(C_i, C_j) | e_{ij} = cosine similarity of news-coverage row vectors (company x article counts)

claim: Negative sentiment shocks propagate asymmetrically; NFL event-study gate. Key propagation pattern: in Group 1 (financials) negative sentiment shocks propagate to neighbors significantly while positive ones do not; same asymmetry in Groups 3, 5, 6; symmetric only in consumer groups 2 and 4. TRUST-SIGNAL lesson recorded: this calibrates how to weight negative vs positive NFL news sentiment (negative QB news moves markets more). Event-study discipline recorded: manual causality check sampling event-day articles to exclude pure market-commentary pieces - guards against circularity in sports news sentiment. Recorded NFL adaptation: build an NFL news co-occurrence network (entities = teams/players from ESPN/beat-writer text; Louvain groups ~= divisions/conferences) with entity-level daily sentiment and run an event study on line moves, gating adoption on whether QB sentiment events move lines beyond official injury-designation dummies (1-2 weeks effort per the ledger).

Predicting next-day implied-volatility direction from market + alternative data with walk-forward validation. Dierckx, Davis & Schoutens (KU Leuven), arXiv:2009.07947 - predicts next-day direction of AAPL implied volatility from 78 engineered features (market + Google News counts + Wikipedia page views) with walk-forward validation. Target: y_i^* = ivol_{i+1} - ivol_i; y_i = 1 iff y_i^* > 0 (eq. 2); class split 59% down / 41% up. Stationarity: Augmented Dickey-Fuller per feature; first-difference non-stationary ones. Models (sklearn defaults, no tuning): Logistic Regression, RBF-SVM (standardized, 29-feature AdaBoost-importance subset), AdaBoost (no standardization/selection); no deep learning (too few points); no Random Forests (authors argue random sampling clashes with sequential data). Evaluation: Walk-Forward Validation - 379-day (78%) train window, next day OOS, 106 train-test splits; standardization + feature selection re-run inside each fold; metric = balanced accuracy (mean per-class recall). Ablation: 5 scenarios - (1) market only, (2) news+wiki only, (3) market+wiki, (4) market+news, (5) all. Data: Yahoo Finance (OHLC/volume); personal end-of-day option data (not shared, used for VIX-formula implied vol); Google News daily keyword counts (scraped); Wikimedia API daily 'Apple Inc' page views; 486 daily feature vectors, Jan 1 2016 - Dec 31 2017, AAPL; 78 features/day after technical-indicator expansion (MA/EMA/ROC/Disparity/Momentum n in {3,5,10}, RSI(14), Williams %R(14), Stochastic(14), replicating Weng et al. 2017). No code or data links. Recorded verdict ADAPT - GSE analog is predicting line-movement direction for bet-timing (fire now vs wait for the close).
equation: y_i^* = ivol_{i+1} - ivol_i; y_i = 1 iff y_i^* > 0 | VIX = 100 * sqrt[(2/T) sum_i (Delta K_i/K_i^2) e^{RT} Q(K_i) - (1/T)(F/K_0 - 1)^2]

claim: Alt-data value can hide in model-class interaction; walk-forward discipline for backtests. Recorded lessons: ablation honesty - alt-data value can hide in model-class interaction (LR 52.8% vs AdaBoost 63.0% on identical market+wiki features) - ablate per model class, not just per feature set (TRUST-SIGNAL). Walk-forward + in-fold preprocessing discipline as evaluation template; audit GSE backtest pipelines for full-sample standardization look-ahead (TRUST-SIGNAL). Wikipedia page-traffic as a non-linear attention feature is a candidate alt-data signal for NFL line moves. Recorded GSE plan: build a line-movement-direction model (target = sign(close - current) on spread/total, market features + alt data like X volume/news counts/Wikipedia views, 78-style technical expansion on line series) under strict walk-forward evaluation with in-fold preprocessing re-fit, gated on >50% OOS balanced accuracy, to decide bet-timing (fire now vs wait).

PlackettLuce package: generalized Plackett-Luce for subset rankings with ties, pseudo-comparisons, quasi-SEs, PL trees. Full-text ledger (read 2026-09-21) of the software paper for the R PlackettLuce package (Turner, van Etten, Firth, Kosmidis; JSS, arXiv:1810.12068v2). Generalized PL likelihood over (possibly tied, subset) rankings with Davidson-Luce tie handling (tie probability proportional to delta * geometric-mean-of-worths-type terms; exact form in the paper). Pseudo-comparisons: augmented likelihood adds weight-0.5 pseudo-wins/losses vs a hypothetical average-worth item -> finite MLEs in disconnected networks, shrinks worths toward equality. Quasi-variances: qvar_i such that Var(log what_i - log what_j) approx qvar_i + qvar_j, reference-free contrast uncertainty. PL trees: recursive partitioning on ranking-level covariates via parameter-instability tests to find subgroups with different worth structures. Data: NASCAR example (36 races, 87 drivers, 42-43 per race; data included in the package); synthetic benchmark of 5,000 sub-rankings of 10 items from 100 with ties to order 4, fit 18.1s / covariance 14.8s on a 2.10 GHz i7 / 16 GB. R package PlackettLuce (CRAN). Paper itself is the method source; R-only, GSE stack would need a port. Explicit warnings: PL trees can be unstable (paper's own warning); high-order ties grow combinatorially in memory/time; online/streaming estimation and spatiotemporal extensions listed as future work, not implemented. No predictive baseline comparison - validation is correctness + performance (software paper). Corpus gap noted: Plackett-Luce only 'mentioned, not deeply researched' in the existing-research map; pseudo-comparisons and quasi-SEs absent from the map. Recorded verdict ADAPT - the pseudo-comparison trick solves GSE's early-season disconnected-rating problem and quasi-SEs give reference-free rating uncertainty.

Pseudo-comparison regularization for early-season disconnected ratings. Intelligence connections recorded: pseudo-comparison regularization (weight-0.5 pseudo-games vs league-average team) for early-season/disconnected ratings - directly matches GSE's September ratings gap (SCHEME/TRUST-SIGNAL); quasi-SEs removing reference-team arbitrariness in published rating uncertainty (TRUST-SIGNAL); PL trees as a principled regime-split finder on pick history with market/regime covariates (unstable per paper's warning) (OTHER); Davidson-Luce arbitrary-order tie handling (OTHER, e.g., fantasy finish ties). Recorded plan: port pseudo-comparisons into GSE's pairwise rating models (weight-0.5 pseudo-games vs league-average team to stabilize early-season ratings) and quasi-SEs for published rating uncertainty, with the adoption gate being regularized early-season NFL ratings beating unregularized on weeks 5-8 held-out log-likelihood (~1 week effort per the ledger).

FPL skill-vs-luck instruments: skill persistence, transfer-regret metric, template-team detection. O'Brien, Gleeson & O'Sullivan, arXiv:2009.01206v1 - asks whether fantasy success is skill or luck using 901,912 FPL managers' full 2018/19 season, isolating: season-to-season skill persistence, top-tier transfer quality, chip timing, and template-team herding via co-occurrence clustering. Skill persistence: pairwise Pearson correlations of season points totals across 13 seasons; OLS of 2018/19 points on number of prior seasons played. 'Fraction of better transfers possible' y_G(x_i,x_j) = sum_k 1[q_G(x_k)<=q_G(x_i)] * 1[p_G(x_k)>p_G(x_j)] / sum_l 1[q_G(x_l)<=q_G(x_i)] (perfect-foresight transfer-regret metric). Template team: player co-occurrence matrix A^G_ij (# teams containing both i and j); hierarchical clustering (k=4, elbow on WSS); Jaccard similarity J^G(i,j) = |T_i intersect T_j|/|T_i union T_j| between manager squads (100 teams x 10,000 resamples per tier-pair per GW). Financial cognizance: OLS of final points on team value at each GW; chip strategy: timing distributions + point returns by tier; tier analysis: disjoint tiers by final rank (top 10^3/10^4/10^5/10^6) with per-GW mean-point deltas. Data: FPL 2018/19: 901,912 managers with full-season data (from ~1M top-ranked; ~50M API calls to fantasy.premierleague.com endpoints: entry/event/picks, bootstrap-static, history); historical ~6M managers in 2019/20, ~3.8M with >=1 prior season, 13 seasons of pairwise overlap. No code links. Recorded verdict ADAPT - three portable instruments: template-team (chalk) detection, a transfer-regret decision-quality metric for GSE's optimizer/waiver logic, and skill-persistence correlations to calibrate real DFS edge vs noise.
equation: y_G(x_i,x_j) = sum_k 1[q_G(x_k)<=q_G(x_i)] * 1[p_G(x_k)>p_G(x_j)] / sum_l 1[q_G(x_l)<=q_G(x_i)] | J^G(i,j) = |T_i intersect T_j| / |T_i union T_j|

claim: Preparation gap and long-horizon chip planning dominate fantasy success. Process findings: the largest tier gaps appear at GW1 (top-10^3 averaged 88.16 vs 63.17 - preparation before a ball is kicked dominates), plus DGW35 and BGW33. Long-horizon chip sequencing (Free Hit DGW32 -> Wildcard GW34 -> Bench Boost DGW35) beats per-week optimization: 79.4% of top-10k played Bench Boost in DGW35 vs 28.9% of the rest, returns 23.2 vs 13.8 points. Template team: 3 smallest clusters contain only 5.13% (32/624) of players yet anchor most squads; Jaccard similarity rises with tier and oscillates - consensus forms then dissolves. Recorded GSE ports: template-team detection via co-occurrence clustering = formal DFS chalk measurement; transfer-regret metric y_G ported to audit GSE's optimizer/waiver swaps (fraction of same-salary-or-cheaper alternatives that outscored the pick, tracked as weekly CCDF) as a decision-quality KPI; skill-persistence correlations (0.42) to calibrate real edge vs noise before scaling stakes; GW1 preparation gap as process lesson for the weekly DFS packet prep cadence; long-horizon sequencing as season-long/milestone-game planning analog. Recorded gate: build a per-slate chalk meter (ownership-weighted co-occurrence clustering -> template concentration, published in the weekly DFS packet) with a contrarian tilt trigger on top-quartile concentration slates; adopt the transfer-regret metric as a weekly decision-quality KPI; gate on >=10% higher ROI for template-fading vs template-following lineups on top-quartile slates, paired by slate, p<0.05.

Deep similarity learning for team ranking: Siamese contrastive/triplet embeddings into LambdaRank/pairwise boosters. Yazbek et al., 2021, arXiv:2103.13736 - 'Deep Similarity Learning for Sports Team Ranking': tests whether Siamese networks (contrastive and triplet loss) feeding LightGBM LambdaRank / XGBoost pairwise rankers improve end-of-season team ranking prediction in NBA (2014-2018) and Super 15 Rugby (2017-2020) vs the boosters alone. Contrastive loss: J(theta) = (1-Y)(1/2)(D_{a,b})^2 + (Y)(1/2)(max(0, m-D_{a,b}))^2, Y=0 win / 1 loss; D_{a,b} = Euclidean distance between embeddings. Triplet loss: J(theta) = max(D(a,p) - D(a,n) + m, 0); anchor a, positive p (same class), negative n (different class). Gradient boosting updates: F_0(x) = argmin_gamma sum_i L(y_i, gamma); pseudo-residuals r_im = -dL/dF_{m-1}; F_m = F_{m-1} + lambda_m gamma_m h_m(x). mAP = (1/N) sum_i AP_i; Spearman r_s = 1 - 6 sum d_i^2/(n(n^2-1)); nDCG_p = DCG_p/IDCG_p with DCG_p = sum_i (2^{rel_i}-1)/log_2(i+1), relevance 15 (1st) -> 1 (15th). Tally rank: predicted game similarity score added to a team's tally on predicted win, subtracted on loss; tallies sorted descending -> standings. XGBoost pairwise log loss: F = -(1/N) sum_i [y_i log(yhat_i) + (1-y_i)log(1-yhat_i)]. Data: Rugby4cast and Statbunker (rugby); basketball datasets from Thabtah et al. 2019 / Ahmadalinezhad et al. 2019. NBA 2014-2018 (2,460 games/season, 30 teams, 14 box-score features per side); Super 15 Rugby 2017-2020 (120 games/season, 15 teams, 38 seasonal team statistics). Verdict recorded ADAPT.

Leakage caution: end-of-season aggregates predicting same-season games. TRUST-SIGNAL flag recorded: the paper's leakage flaw - end-of-season aggregate stats used to predict games within that same season - overstates true forecasting power. Related observations: no consistent best model across sports (no free lunch; sport-specific validation required); tally-rank aggregation is heuristic, not learned (aggregation-layer opportunity). Recorded GSE plan: learn NFL team-strength embeddings via triplet loss (anchor, beat-team, lost-to-team) from nflverse 2015-2021, freeze, then augment the game-prediction stack with embedding distances; numeric gate: >=0.008 log-loss improvement on 2022-2025 or embedding power ranking Spearman >=0.75 vs final standings in >=3 of 4 seasons (file-level impl spec sections 11-14, effort ~1 week).

next-gen-scraPy: recovering NFL pass locations from NGS pass-chart images via computer vision. Mallepalle, Yurko, Pelechrinis, Ventura (2019), arXiv:1906.03339 - builds a computer-vision pipeline to recover raw pass locations from NFL Next Gen Stats pass-chart images, then models league/QB/defense completion-percentage surfaces by field location and derives CPAE (completion percentage above expectation). Image pipeline: K-Means++ clustering to identify passes/field locations -> DBSCAN noise removal; greedy record linkage validates against Big Data Bowl tracking. Shrinkage surface (2-D Naive Bayes): Phat*_G(Complete|x,y) = [N_g*fhat_g(x,y)*Phat_g + N_Median*fhat_NFL(x,y)*Phat_NFL] / [N_g*fhat_g(x,y) + N_Median*fhat_NFL(x,y)] - weight shifts from league prior to group data as attempts N_g grow. CPAE_g = integral_X integral_Y Phat*_{g,league}(Complete|x,y) * fhat_g(x,y) dx dy (spatial-density-weighted integral of above-league-average completion surface). League-wide completion: GAM for P(Complete|x,y) smooth in distance-from-LOS and distance-from-field-center; attempt density via 2-D KDE. Data: NGS pass-chart images scraped from nextgenstats.nfl.com (2017-2018, 500+ games); >27,000 passes modeled; validation via NFL Big Data Bowl tracking data (first six weeks of 2017). Code + dataset: https://github.com/ryurko/next-gen-scrapy. Verdict recorded ADOPT.
equation: Phat*_G(Complete|x,y) = [N_g*fhat_g(x,y)*Phat_g + N_Median*fhat_NFL(x,y)*Phat_NFL] / [N_g*fhat_g(x,y) + N_Median*fhat_NFL(x,y)] | CPAE_g = integral_X integral_Y Phat*_{g,league}(Complete|x,y) * fhat_g(x,y) dx dy

claim: Open-data replication of proprietary NGS CPAE as verifiable benchmark. TRUST-SIGNAL finding recorded: rho = 0.91 match with official NGS CPAE from public data with a strictly weaker model (no play context) - open-data replication of a proprietary metric, a verifiable benchmark. QB-BEHAVIOR: CPAE stability 0.41 year-over-year - QB accuracy is a persistent but noisy skill (selection bias caveat noted). SCHEME: 4 of top 5 CPAE defenses made the 2018 playoffs - pass-defense quality as playoff-correlated team signal; league-wide completion-by-location profile (deep sidelines 22.7% vs deep middle 30.5%) as route/area value priors. Recorded plan: replicate the open-data CPAE pipeline (league GAM + KDE + Naive Bayes shrinkage) on nflverse pass data as a verifiable QB/defense benchmark; acceptance gate rho >= 0.80 vs official NGS CPAE on a full season; improvement path: condition GAM on down/distance/pressure and test whether context-conditioned CPAE beats raw CPAE at predicting next-season EPA/dropback (~1 day core pipeline).

Self-affirmation feedback models of soccer goal distributions (additive, multiplicative, coupled). Bittner, Nussbaumer, Janke, Weigel (2006), arXiv:physics/0606016v1 - 'Football fever: goal distributions and non-Gaussian statistics': fits soccer goal distributions with microscopic 'self-affirmation' feedback models (scoring changes subsequent scoring probability) rather than ad-hoc Poisson/NBD/GEV. Model A (additive feedback): p(n) = p_0 + n*kappa; Model B (multiplicative): p(n) = p_0*kappa^n (clipped to [0,1]); Model C (coupled): home goal -> p_h x kappa_h, p_a / kappa_a and vice versa. Exact distribution via Pascal recurrence: P_N(n) = [1-p(n)]P_{N-1}(n) + p(n-1)P_{N-1}(n-1), O(N^2), N=90 Bernoulli steps. Continuum limit of Model A = NBD with r = p_0/kappa, p = 1 - e^(-kappa*N) (Appendix A proof). GEV: P_{xi,mu,sigma}(n) = (1/sigma)[1 + xi(n-mu)/sigma]^(-1-1/xi) exp(-[1 + xi(n-mu)/sigma]^(-1/xi)). Sum/difference consistency: P_Sigma(sigma) = sum_n P_h(n)P_a(sigma-n); P_Delta(delta) via modified Bessel I_delta (Poisson case). Data: fussballdaten.de, fussballportal.de, nordostfussball.de, sportergebnisse.de, rdasilva.demon.co.uk; Bundesliga 1963/64-2004/05 (~12,800 matches), Oberliga (GDR) 1949/50-1990/91 (~7,700), Frauen-Bundesliga 1997/98-2004/05 (~1,050), FIFA World Cup qualification 1930-2002 (~3,400), plus 14 further European premier leagues. Verdict recorded ADAPT.
equation: Model A: p(n) = p_0 + n*kappa; Model B: p(n) = p_0*kappa^n (clipped to [0,1]); Model C: home goal -> p_h x kappa_h, p_a / kappa_a and vice versa | P_N(n) = [1-p(n)]P_{N-1}(n) + p(n-1)P_{N-1}(n-1), O(N^2), N=90 Bernoulli steps | Continuum limit of Model A = NBD with r = p_0/kappa, p = 1 - e^(-kappa*N)

claim: Poisson rejected for soccer goals; multiplicative feedback and spurious-contagion caveat. Poisson is rejected everywhere (chi^2/dof 6.53-12.8; tails fatter than Poisson); NBD fits well (0.68-4.09); Model B (multiplicative feedback) fits World Cup qualification extremely well, away scores better than GEV. GEV never best for German leagues (xi small, mostly negative Weibull; Gumbel rejected). Weak but significant negative home-away correlation: R = -0.031+-0.009 (Bundesliga). Caveat [37] recorded: NBD arises both as compound-Poisson (non-contagious) and as the limit of contagious Model A - fit quality alone cannot prove the feedback mechanism (spurious contagion). Recorded GSE ports: replace Poisson totals modeling with multiplicative feedback model B (exact O(N^2) recurrence, one kappa per league), gate: feedback model must beat Poisson by >=4 chi^2/dof points before use in totals pricing; immediate application: multiplicative in-play totals updates after each goal plus a spread/total coherence gate (sum/difference convolution consistency check as template: flag inconsistent score-difference distributions - TRUST-SIGNAL). Per-league kappa profiling as league-level scoring-feedback priors for low-data leagues; kappa interpretation ('more encouraging' scoring vs defensive-mode-when-leading) as in-play behavioral read (COACHING).

Classification with reject option via conformal prediction: distribution-free singleton error guarantees. Szabadvary et al. (Jonkoeping U., 2025), arXiv:2506.21802v1 - formalizes conformal prediction as a binary classifier with reject option and derives the correct distribution-free singleton error rate for the offline inductive setting. Reject rule: m(x,eps) = reject-empty if |Gamma^eps(x)|=0 (novelty rejection); accept Gamma^eps(x) if |Gamma^eps(x)|=1; = reject-ambiguous if |Gamma^eps(x)|=2 (ambiguity rejection). Accept iff eps in I_x = [gamma_x, c_x). Proposition 2 (online smoothed CP): sigma := P(err | S) = (eps - P(E)) / P(S); estimator sigmahat = (n*eps - e)/s -> sigma a.s.; error rate = sigma; reject rate = 1 - P(S). Bounds P(E) <= eps <= 1 - P(D) hold, so sigma in [0,1]. Offline ICP correction (the paper's key fix): eps_tilde = eps - sqrt(ln(1/delta)/(2h)) with calibration size h; singleton bound sigma_tilde = (eps_tilde - P(E))/P(S), estimated by (n*eps_tilde - e)/s - a PAC-type guarantee with two parameters (prior papers used the online formula offline, only approximately correct). Mondrian (label-conditional): sigma_k = (eps_k - P(E_k))/P(S_k), estimated (n_k eps_k - e_k)/s_k per category. Batch offline ICP: sigma_tilde_k = (N_k eps_tilde_k - e_k)/s_k per batch; -> sigma as batches accumulate (delta_{k+1} = delta_k^{h_{k+1}/h_k}). Assumptions: exchangeable data sequence (weaker than i.i.d.); binary labels (multiclass via one-vs-all); smoothed CP; nested prediction sets in eps. Data: three numerical demos on public UCI-style sets: qsar-biodeg (1055x41), spambase (4601x57), California-Housing-Classification (20640x8). Tooling: Crepes (inductive conformal prediction). No author code released. Verdict recorded ADAPT as the abstention lane's theoretical anchor.
equation: m(x,eps) = reject-empty if |Gamma^eps(x)|=0; accept Gamma^eps(x) if |Gamma^eps(x)|=1; reject-ambiguous if |Gamma^eps(x)|=2 | sigma = P(err | S) = (eps - P(E)) / P(S); sigmahat = (n*eps - e)/s | eps_tilde = eps - sqrt(ln(1/delta)/(2h)); sigma_tilde = (eps_tilde - P(E))/P(S) estimated by (n*eps_tilde - e)/s

claim: Conformal abstention operating discipline and honest limits. Operational rules recorded: error-reject curves parameterized by eps; same reject rate can arise from different eps -> always pick the smallest eps (lowest error); desk picks operating points like 'publish only singletons at eps giving <=8% error'. Honest limits: not all reject rates achievable; the guarantee is weakest under distribution shift - precisely when abstention is most needed (novelty rejections route to analyst review). Mondrian per-category guarantees sigma_k condition on league/market type for label-conditional pick guarantees. Recorded GSE plan: build a conformal abstention gate on the pick pipeline - wrap the win-probability model in offline ICP (calibration = recent closed picks), publish only singleton sets, report guaranteed singleton error sigma_tilde per slate; numeric gate: reproduce the spambase experiment and require empirical singleton error <= corrected bound sigma_tilde in >=95% of 1000 runs at eps=0.10, h=500, delta=0.05, AND confirm the uncorrected formula fails the gate; improvement: validate on 2+ seasons of GSE binary picks (published singletons >=3pp lower error than published-all at <=40% reject).

Fast rates for online prediction with abstention: no-bet option turns sqrt(T) regret into log N. Neu & Zhivotovskiy (2020), arXiv:2001.10623 - 'Fast Rates for Online Prediction with Abstention': pure-theory paper proving that a no-bet option at cost c < 1/2 turns regret from growing sqrt(T) into a horizon-independent log N bound. Theorem 1: R_T <= log N / eta, with eta = 2(1-2c). Abstention rule: predict weighted-majority class k*_t with confidence p*_t; abstain with probability alpha_t = 2(1-p*_t). Expected loss: E[lhat_t] = alpha_t*c + (1-alpha_t)*1{k*_t != y_t}. Lemma 4 proof step: E[lhat_t] = r_t - (1-2c)(r_t wedge (1-r_t)), where r_t = sum_i q_{t,i} 1{y_{t,i} != y_t}. Corollary 2: tuning eta gives R_T <= (log N)/(2(1-2c)) wedge sqrt(T log N / 2). Matching lower bound of order log N/(1-2c) - tight. Extensions: time-varying costs c_t <= 1/2 (Proposition 5); Tsybakov-type margin condition (1/T) sum_t 1{1/2 - c_t < x} <= beta x^{alpha/(1-alpha)} (Definition 6) yielding R_T = O((log N)^{1/(2-alpha)} T^{(1-alpha)/(2-alpha)}) (Corollary 7). No datasets, no experiments, no code - pure theory. Acceptance gate (ledger): ADOPT only if the alpha-rule's cumulative regret vs best expert over 2024 is <= 50% of the publish-all rule's AND no-bet rate <= 40%. Verdict recorded ADAPT as the theoretical backbone for GSE's selective-publishing (no-bet) layer.
equation: R_T <= log N / eta, eta = 2(1-2c) | alpha_t = 2(1-p*_t) | E[lhat_t] = alpha_t*c + (1-alpha_t)*1{k*_t != y_t}

claim: Selective-publishing implementation: publish only above consensus threshold. Recorded implementation: publish only when weighted consensus p* >= (1-tau/2), tau calibrated on 2024 to a target no-bet rate; one-line aggregation change per the ledger. Other recorded uses: exponential-weight no-bet rule with abstention probability alpha_t = 2(1-p*_t) over engine model variants + signal experts - implementable one-line aggregation addition (<1 day per ledger); slate-adaptive costs - skip more aggressively on thin slates, less on full slates (maps to the Tsybakov time-varying-cost section); first-principles justification for the abstention/selective-publishing lane - cumulative regret flattening is the fast-rate signature to verify on 2024 time-ordered data (TRUST-SIGNAL).

Gate-Shift-Pose: skeleton-pose fusion into Gate-Shift-Fuse RGB action recognition. Bianchi & Lanz (2025), arXiv:2503.04470 - adds skeleton pose (YOLO11-x-pose) to a Gate-Shift-Fuse RGB action-recognition network via early-fusion (Gaussian heatmap as 4th input channel) or late-fusion (two-stream + multi-head attention) for binary athlete fall classification in figure skating. Early-fusion: X = [RGB; H(keypoints)], H = sum_j exp(-||p-k_j||^2/2 sigma^2) (formalized from text, no numbered loss equations in paper). Late-fusion: z = MHA(concat(L2(f_RGB), L2(f_pose))), pose MLP 34-dim -> FC64 -> FC128 -> FC128, then FC halve-dim -> BN -> ReLU -> dropout twice (FC1 64, FC2 32) -> FC classifier; cross-entropy loss. Backbones ResNet18/ResNet50 (ImageNet init); SGD momentum 0.9, wd 5e-4, LR 0.01 cosine annealing, batch {4,8}, segments {16,32}, 120 epochs. Design rule from results: early-fusion wins with large backbones, late-fusion wins with light backbones. Data: FR-FS dataset: 417 video samples (276 fall, 141 non-fall), 103 frames each, from the FIV dataset + PyeongChang 2018 Winter Olympics footage. YOLO11-x-pose (COCO, 17 keypoints; mAP 69.5% @ 0.5:0.95, 91.1% @ 0.5; 58.8M params); keypoints precomputed to disk. Project page: https://edowhite.github.io/Gate-Shift-Pose. Ledger verdict ADAPT with a numeric gate. Leakage flag: train/val split protocol not described (same athletes may appear in both splits); baselines likely undertrained, inflating gain claims.
equation: X = [RGB; H(keypoints)], H = sum_j exp(-||p-k_j||^2 / 2 sigma^2) | z = MHA(concat(L2(f_RGB), L2(f_pose)))

claim: Fusion-strategy-vs-backbone rule with athlete-disjoint validation gate. Design rule recorded: early-fusion wins with large backbones, late-fusion wins with light backbones - directly usable design rule for GSE RGB+pose classifiers; ResNet18 late-fusion for edge/latency-constrained deployment. Gaussian-heatmap-as-4th-channel is a cheap way to inject pose into any 2D video CNN without a graph network - applies to GSE binary technique-event classifiers (clean vs awkward landing, injury cues from broadcast). TRUST-SIGNAL: split-hygiene warning - athlete-disjoint 5-fold CV required before trusting gains. Numeric gate (ledger): both GSP variants must beat RGB-only by >=10pp on athlete-disjoint folds, and the fusion/backbone ranking must hold, before the design rule ships. Engine plan: for any GSE binary motion-event classifier on broadcast clips: ResNet50-GSF early-fusion 4-channel when compute allows, ResNet18 late-fusion attention stream for edge; poses precomputed offline with YOLO11-pose, sweep segments {16,32} x batch {4,8}.

Joint inference of latent skills and the unknown monotone win-probability kernel (EM + belief propagation). Sanchez Catalina & Cantwell, arXiv:2512.15269v1 - 'Model inference for ranking from pairwise comparisons': jointly infers latent skills AND the unknown monotone win-probability kernel from data via EM + belief propagation, instead of assuming the logistic kernel. Latent skills s_i; win-probability kernel p(s_i - s_j) unknown, constrained monotone increasing. Kernel parametrizations: (i) Chebyshev polynomial expansion of the log-odds curve; (ii) neural network with monotonicity constraints. EM: E-step runs belief propagation over the match graph for posterior skill marginals; M-step updates kernel parameters. Baselines: fixed-logistic Bradley-Terry/Elo - compared on skill RMSE (synthetic) and log-loss (ATP prediction). Data: synthetic 1,024 players x 64 matches each with known ground-truth kernel (identifiability check); eleven real pairwise-comparison datasets (sports and non-sports); ledger gives no headline numerics beyond qualitative 'good fit'. ATP tour: fit 2021-2022, predict 2023-2024 from prior-12-month observations, strictly chronological. Authors' code: https://github.com/gcant/pairwise-comparison-inference. GSE overlap note: corpus inventories Elo, Glicko, TrueSkill, Bradley-Terry, Plackett-Luce as known methods - all fix the kernel a priori; this paper is the only joint skill-plus-kernel method in the tracked corpus. Ledger verdict ADAPT. Numeric gate (ledger): ADAPT iff learned kernel beats fixed logistic on GSE's own backtest - lower log-loss on at least two held-out NFL seasons; if the learned kernel collapses to logistic, adaptation adds nothing.

Logistic kernel as an untested assumption of the rating layer. Core lesson recorded: GSE's rating layer inherits the logistic kernel as an untested assumption; learning the kernel per sport captures favorite-longshot asymmetries and diminishing returns to large skill gaps that a fixed sigmoid misses. TRUST-SIGNAL: learned-kernel tail deviations quantify favorite-longshot bias / chalk compression - directly usable as a calibration correction on GSE probability outputs (feeds the calibration layer). Extensions recorded: learn score-differential kernel for margin-of-victory (ordered outcomes), or separate kernels per segment (divisional vs non-divisional, playoff vs regular season); success criterion is log-loss + ECE wins on NFL 2022-2025.

NBA expansion travel-fairness optimization: travel minimization (M1) and Nash bargaining (M2). Hassanzadeh, Davari & Goossens, arXiv:2512.16968v1 - two optimization models (pure travel minimization M1, Nash-bargaining fairness M2) over conference/division realignment for a 32-team NBA, evaluated across 15 expansion city pairings under 82/72-game x 2/4-division scenarios. Theory distance: opponent distances weighted by expected game frequency from division/conference structure; regression vs 2004-2018 actual travel gives R^2 approx 0.34 (in-sample - calibration, not validation). M1: minimize total theory travel (assignment MIP). M2: Nash bargaining - displayed as minimizing sum_i log(w_i), w_i = team i's travel-increase ratio vs baseline (ledger flags: text describes product maximization; displayed form maximizes product(1/w_i), pushing each increase ratio toward 1 - verify intended bargaining semantics before reusing M2 verbatim). Constraint: market exposure (metropolitan population proxy) >= gamma=0.8 of baseline per team. Scenario grid: {82, 72} games x {2, 4} divisions/conference x 15 pairings from six candidate cities (Seattle, Las Vegas, Montreal, Vancouver, Tampa, Mexico City). Data: NBA team geography; 2004-2018 actual travel (regression validation); metropolitan populations (market proxy); media-market universe estimates. No code stated in the paper. Limitations (authors): no back-to-back or long-road-trip modeling; distance != fatigue (no sports-science integration); fairness only via Nash bargaining (no max-min/CVaR). Ledger verdict ADAPT - reusable optimization template and travel-burden fatigue features.
equation: minimize sum_i log(w_i), w_i = team i travel-increase ratio vs baseline | market exposure >= gamma = 0.8 of baseline per team

claim: Theory-distance travel-burden features with rest-day interaction. Recorded uses: theory-distance calculator -> team travel burden and travel-burden differential as fatigue features for the NBA game model, interacting with ledger-1059 rest/travel coefficients. M1/M2 template lets GSE audit any released schedule for competitive fairness (who bears the travel burden) - modeling + content value. TRUST-SIGNAL: fairness finding - constraining burden-fairness costs only ~23 miles in 2.58M, i.e., fairness is cheap in aggregate; useful framing for schedule-fairness content. Caveat recorded: distance != fatigue; back-to-backs and road-trip-length structure are missing (authors flag this), so raw miles must be combined with rest-day features rather than used alone. Numeric gate (ledger): ADAPT iff travel-burden differential (theory distance over trailing N days) improves GSE's NBA game model on rolling-origin log-loss beyond the ledger-1059 rest/travel features.

Ignorance (log) score vs Brier and RPS for football outcome forecasts. Full-read ledger of Wheatcroft (arXiv:1908.08980v1), which argues against the Ranked Probability Score for football outcome forecasts and shows via two experiments that the ignorance (log) score identifies the true forecasting system faster and more reliably than Brier and RPS. Brier = sum_i(p_i - o_i)^2 (eq. 1); RPS = sum_{i=1}^{r-1} sum_{j=1}^i (p_j - o_j)^2 (eq. 2); IGN = -log_2(p(Y)) (eq. 3). Properties: all three proper; only ignorance is local; only RPS is distance-sensitive; equitable/regular/feasible defined. Experiment 1: perfect vs imperfect forecast pairs over n repeated draws; selection = lower mean score; P(select perfect) vs n. Experiment 2: imperfection delta: eps = (1/3)(|ptilde_h-p_h|+|ptilde_d-p_d|+|ptilde_a-p_a|) (eq. 4); imperfect forecast drawn from {eps<delta}; pairwise differences with 95% resampling intervals. Odds->probabilities (App. B, eq. 5): p_h = (1/O_h)/sum_i(1/O_i) - margin removed by renormalization; max odds across bookmakers used. Mean relative ignorance Delta (bits) iff 2^Delta = mean increase in probability density placed on the outcome. Data: football-data.co.uk: 39,343 matches, top five English leagues 2005/06 onward (EPL 6,460; Championship/League One/League Two 6,624 each; National League 6,488). Synthetic five Constantinou-Fenton forecast pairs (Experiment 1). Findings: hierarchy ignorance > Brier > RPS at low imperfection (delta=0.01, 0.025; 95% resampling intervals exclude zero for large n); ignorance still significantly better at delta=0.05, 0.1. Experiment 1: ignorance identifies the perfect system fastest for almost all n; RPS barely improves with n on match 4. Verdict in file: ADAPT.
equation: Brier = sum_i(p_i - o_i)^2 | RPS = sum_{i=1}^{r-1} sum_{j=1}^i (p_j - o_j)^2 | IGN = -log_2(p(Y))

claim: Ignorance as primary engine-variant selection metric with 0.05-bit gate. Ledger's numeric gate recorded: adopt ignorance as GSE's primary engine-variant selection metric; promote a challenger only if mean relative ignorance >= 0.05 bits (2^0.05 approx 1.035x mean probability placed on the outcome) on held-out games with 95% resampling interval of the pairwise difference excluding zero. Intelligence connections recorded: 2^Delta bits interpretation as gambler-legible publishable stat (TRUST-SIGNAL, public model-card transparency); caveat that the hierarchy is proven for near-perfect discrimination, not the messy middle of imperfect-vs-imperfect (methodological limitation). Plan: make mean ignorance (log_2) the engine-variant selection metric per the paper's two experiments.

WiDIR: wide-and-deep multi-branch learning-to-rank for personalized fantasy contest recommendation. Srilakshmi et al. (arXiv:2508.14065v1) - WiDIR, a wide-and-deep multi-branch learning-to-rank model for personalized fantasy contest recommendation on Dream11, validated on ~1B joins and a 4-arm online A/B test. WiDIR: wide linear branch (memorizes feature interactions) + three deep branches - player tower, contest tower, player-contest interaction tower - embeddings concatenated into a final scoring layer. Pairwise hinge loss: max(0, 1 - s_i(c) + s_i(c')), where s_i(c) is the score of contest c for user i and c' is a lower-ranked contest. Offline evaluation: precision/recall at 1, 3, 5, 10. Online: 4-arm A/B (control, Popular, LightGBM ranker, WiDIR), 1M players per cohort, 6 weeks. Serving: rankings within 10 ms; inference restricted to users active in the previous month. Data: Dream11 production data (proprietary): train ~1B joins, 100k players, 1.5M contests; test ~0.5B joins, 100k players, 0.9M contests; ~12 mo train / 2 mo validation / 6 mo test, time-ordered. Features: 107 player features, 11 contest features, 9 player-contest interaction features. Candidate list fixed at 100 contests (50/100/200 evaluated). Findings: WiDIR beat Popular and LightGBM offline (P/R@k) and won the online A/B - the paper reports the win via plots only; exact numeric lifts not stated in text (chart-read only). Scale: ~1B training joins; serving latency <=10 ms; inference cohort = users active in the previous month. Verdict in file: ADAPT (product), not for the prediction engine.

WiDIR product adaptation for personalized pick feed with GBM gate. Recorded: No for the prediction engine; yes for product - adapt the WiDIR architecture (not weights) for GSE's personalized pick-feed/notification ranking with a pairwise hinge loss on engagement logs, with a >=5% relative P/R@5 gate over LightGBM before adoption. Caveats recorded: 1B-join scale validates the design but advantage demonstrated only at that scale (transfer risk); exact numeric lifts chart-read only, not stated in text. Improvement recorded: add calibration head (isotonic/Platt) to convert rankings to P(join) thresholds (TRUST-SIGNAL, calibrated notification expected value).

Rejected read: HistoricalML neuro-symbolic framework for sparse historical data. Kublashvili (arXiv:2512.01723v1), claimed 'HistoricalML' neuro-symbolic framework for sparse historical data (WWI naval arms race, Punic Wars). Verdict in file: REJECT - no genuine validation; replaced by ledger 1306 ('Kelly Betting as Bayesian Model Evaluation').
